And Abram passed through the length of the land, to the place of Shechem, to the high oak. Now the Canaanites lived in the land at that time.
And the Lord appeared to Abram and said to him, “To your seed I will give this land.” And there Abram built an altar to the Lord, who had appeared to him.

And he departed from there to the mountain east of Bethel, and pitched his tent there, with Bethel toward the sea and Ai toward the east. And there he built an altar to the Lord and called upon the name of the Lord.
And Abram departed, and journeyed, and camped in the wilderness.
And there was a famine in the land; and Abram went down into Egypt to stay there, for the famine had become severe in the land.
And when Abram drew near to enter Egypt, Abram said to Sara his wife, “I know that you are a woman with a beautiful face.
When the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife’; and they will kill me, but they will keep you alive.
So say, ‘I am his sister,’ that it may be well with me for your sake, and my soul shall live because of you.”
And when Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.
And Pharaoh’s rulers saw her and praised her to Pharaoh; and they brought her into Pharaoh’s house.
And they treated Abram well for her sake; and he had sheep, and calves, and donkeys, male slaves and female slaves, mules and camels.
And God afflicted Pharaoh and his house with great and grievous afflictions because of Sara, Abram’s wife.
And Pharaoh called Abram and said, “What is this you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she is your wife?
Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her as my wife? And now, look, your wife is before you; take her and hurry away.”
And Pharaoh commanded men to escort Abram away, with his wife and all that he had, and Lot with him.
And Abram went up out of Egypt into the wilderness, he and his wife, and all that he had, and Lot with him.
Now Abram was very rich in livestock, and in silver, and in gold.
And he went back the way he had come, into the wilderness as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been before, between Bethel and Ai,
to the place of the altar, where he had made it at first. And there Abram called upon the name of the Lord.
And Lot also, who journeyed with Abram, had sheep, and cattle, and tents.
And the land could not hold them while they lived together, for their possessions were many; and they could not live together.
And there was strife between the herdsmen of Abram’s livestock and the herdsmen of Lot’s livestock. Now the Canaanites and the Perizzites lived in the land at that time.
And Abram said to Lot, “Let there be no strife between me and you, nor between my herdsmen and your herdsmen; for we are brothers.
Look, is not all the land before you? Separate yourself from me. If you go to the left, I will go to the right; and if you go to the right, I will go to the left.”

And Lot lifted up his eyes and saw all the country around the Jordan, that it was all well watered, before God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, like the garden of God and like the land of Egypt, as far as Zoar.
And Lot chose for himself all the country around the Jordan; and Lot departed from the east, and they separated, each from his brother.
And Abram lived in the land of Canaan; but Lot lived in a city of the surrounding country, and pitched his tent in Sodom.
Now the men of Sodom were exceedingly wicked and sinful before God.
And God said to Abram, after Lot had separated himself from him, “Lift up your eyes and look from the place where you now are, toward the north, and the south, and the east, and the sea.
For all the land that you see I will give to you and to your seed for ever.
And I will make your seed like the sand of the earth. If anyone can count the sand of the earth, then your seed too shall be counted.
Rise, pass through the length and breadth of the land; for I will give it to you.”
And Abram moved his tent, and came and lived beside the oak of Mamre, which was in Hebron; and there he built an altar to the Lord.
And in the reign of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, and Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Thargal king of nations
made war with Balla king of Sodom, and Barsa king of Gomorrah, and Sennaar king of Admah, and Symobor king of Zeboiim, and the king of Balak, which is Zoar.
All these joined together at the salt ravine, which is the Salt Sea.
For twelve years they served Chedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
And in the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer came with the kings who were with him, and struck the giants in Ashteroth-karnaim, and strong nations with them, and the Ommaeans in the city of Shaveh,
and the Horites in the mountains of Seir, as far as the terebinth of Paran, which is in the wilderness.
And they turned back and came to the Spring of Judgment, which is Kadesh; and they struck all the rulers of Amalek, and the Amorites who lived in Hazezon-tamar.
And the king of Sodom, and the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Admah, and the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Balak, which is Zoar, went out and drew up their battle lines in the salt valley
against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Thargal king of nations, and Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar: four kings against five.
Now the salt valley was full of bitumen pits. And the king of Sodom and the king of Gomorrah fled and fell into them; and those who remained fled to the hill country.
And they took all the horses of Sodom and Gomorrah, and all their food, and departed.
And they also took Lot, Abram’s brother’s son, and his baggage, and departed; for he lived in Sodom.

And one of those who escaped came and told Abram, the man from beyond. Now he lived beside the oak of Mamre the Amorite, the brother of Eshcol and the brother of Aunan; and these were sworn allies of Abram.
And when Abram heard that Lot his brother had been taken captive, he counted his own slaves born in his house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them as far as Dan.
And he fell upon them by night, he and his servants, and struck them; and he pursued them as far as Hobah, which is to the left of Damascus.
And he brought back all the horses of Sodom; and he brought back Lot his brother, and his possessions, and the women, and the people.
And the king of Sodom went out to meet him, after his return from the defeat of Chedorlaomer and the kings with him, at the valley of Shaveh, which was the King’s Plain.
And Melchizedek king of Salem brought out loaves and wine; and he was priest of God Most High.
And he blessed Abram and said, “Blessed be Abram by God Most High, who created the heaven and the earth;
and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your power.” And he gave him a tenth of all.
And the king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the men, and take the horses for yourself.”
And Abram said to the king of Sodom, “I will stretch out my hand to God Most High, who created the heaven and the earth,
that I will take neither a thread nor a sandal fastening of anything that is yours, so that you may not say, ‘I have made Abram rich,’
except what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me: Eshcol, Aunan, and Mamre. They shall take a portion.”
After these things the word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Do not fear, Abram; I shield you. Your reward shall be exceedingly great.”
And Abram said, “Master, what wilt Thou give me? I depart childless; and the son of Masek, the slave woman born in my house, is this Damascus Eliezer.”
And Abram said, “Since Thou hast given me no seed, a slave born in my house shall inherit from me.”
And immediately the voice of the Lord came to him, saying, “This man shall not inherit from you; but the one who will come from you, he shall inherit from you.”
And He brought him outside and said to him, “Look now toward heaven, and count the stars, if you can count them.” And He said, “So shall your seed be.”
And Abram believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.
And He said to him, “I am God, who brought you out from the country of the Chaldeans, to give you this land to inherit.”
And he said, “Master Lord, how shall I know that I shall inherit it?”
And He said to him, “Take for Me a heifer three years old, and a female goat three years old, and a ram three years old, and a turtledove, and a pigeon.”
And he took all these for Him, and divided them down the middle, and laid the pieces opposite one another; but he did not divide the birds.
And birds came down upon the bodies, upon their divided pieces; and Abram sat down with them.
And about sunset a trance fell upon Abram; and behold, a great dark fear fell upon him.
And it was said to Abram, “Know for certain that your seed shall live as strangers in a land not their own; and they shall enslave them, and afflict them, and humble them for four hundred years.
But I will judge the nation they serve; and afterward they shall come out here with much baggage.
But you shall depart to your fathers in peace, buried at a good old age.
And in the fourth generation they shall return here; for the sins of the Amorites are not yet filled up.”
And as the sun was setting, a flame appeared; and behold, a smoking furnace, and torches of fire which passed between these divided pieces.
On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, “To your seed I will give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates:
the Kenites, and the Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites,
and the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Rephaim,
and the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Hivites, and the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.”
Now Sara, Abram’s wife, bore him no children; and she had an Egyptian slave woman whose name was Hagar.
And Sara said to Abram, “Look, the Lord has kept me from bearing children. So go in to my slave woman, that you may have children through her.” And Abram listened to the voice of Sara.
And Sara, Abram’s wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her slave woman, after Abram had lived ten years in the land of Canaan, and gave her to Abram her husband to be his wife.
And he went in to Hagar, and she conceived; and she saw that she was with child, and her mistress was dishonoured in her sight.
And Sara said to Abram, “I am wronged by you. I gave my slave woman into your bosom; but when I saw that she was with child, I was dishonoured in her sight. May God judge between me and you.”
And Abram said to Sara, “Look, your slave woman is in your hands; do with her as you please.” And Sara afflicted her, and she fled from her face.
And an angel of the Lord found her by the spring of water in the wilderness, by the spring on the way to Shur.
And the angel of the Lord said to her, “Hagar, Sara’s slave woman, where have you come from, and where are you going?” And she said, “I am fleeing from the face of Sara my mistress.”
And the angel of the Lord said to her, “Return to your mistress, and humble yourself under her hands.”
And the angel of the Lord said to her, “I will greatly multiply your seed, and it shall be too numerous to count.”
And the angel of the Lord said to her, “Behold, you are with child, and shall bear a son, and shall call his name Ishmael, for the Lord has heard your affliction.
He shall be a wild man; his hands shall be against all, and the hands of all against him; and he shall live opposite all his brothers.”
And Hagar called the name of the Lord who spoke to her, “Thou art God who has looked upon me”; for she said, “For I also saw before me Him who appeared to me.”
Therefore she called the well, “The Well Where I Saw Before Me.” Behold, it is between Kadesh and Bered.
And Hagar bore Abram a son; and Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bore to him, Ishmael.
Now Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.
And when Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to Abram and said to him, “I am your God; be pleasing before Me, and be blameless.
And I will set My covenant between Me and you, and will multiply you exceedingly.”
And Abram fell upon his face; and God spoke to him, saying,
“As for Me, behold, My covenant is with you, and you shall be a father of a multitude of nations.
And your name shall no longer be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham; for I have made you a father of many nations.
And I will increase you exceedingly, exceedingly, and will make nations of you; and kings shall come from you.
And I will establish My covenant between Me and you and your seed after you throughout their generations, as an everlasting covenant, to be your God and the God of your seed after you.
And I will give to you, and to your seed after you, the land where you live as a stranger, all the land of Canaan, as an everlasting possession; and I will be their God.”
And God said to Abraham, “And you shall keep My covenant, you and your seed after you throughout their generations.
And this is the covenant that you shall keep, between Me and you, and your seed after you throughout their generations: every male among you shall be circumcised.
And you shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.

And every male child among you, eight days old, shall be circumcised throughout your generations, the slave born in your house, and the slave bought with silver from any foreigner who is not of your seed.
The slave born in your house, and the slave bought with silver, shall surely be circumcised; and My covenant shall be upon your flesh as an everlasting covenant.
And the uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin on the eighth day, that soul shall be destroyed from his kindred; for he has broken My covenant.”
And God said to Abraham, “Sara your wife shall no longer be called Sara, but Sarah shall be her name.
And I will bless her, and will give you a child by her; and I will bless him, and he shall become nations, and kings of nations shall come from him.”
And Abraham fell upon his face and laughed, and said in his mind, “Shall a child be born to a man a hundred years old? And shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?”
And Abraham said to God, “Let this Ishmael live before Thee.”

And God said to Abraham, “Yes; behold, Sarah your wife shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac. And I will establish My covenant with him as an everlasting covenant, and with his seed after him.
And concerning Ishmael, behold, I have heard you. Behold, I have blessed him, and I will increase him and multiply him exceedingly; he shall beget twelve nations, and I will make him a great nation.
But I will establish My covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah shall bear to you at this season next year.”
And He finished speaking with him; and God went up from Abraham.

And Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all the slaves born in his house, and all the slaves bought with silver, every male among the men of Abraham’s house; and he circumcised their foreskins on that very day, as God had spoken to him.
Now Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he circumcised the flesh of his foreskin.
And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
On that very day Abraham and Ishmael his son were circumcised.
And all the men of his house, both the slaves born in his house and the slaves bought with silver from foreign nations, he circumcised.
And God appeared to him beside the oak of Mamre, as he sat at the door of his tent at noon.
And he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, three men stood over him. And when he saw them, he ran from the door of his tent to meet them and bowed to the earth,
and said, “Lord, if indeed I have found grace before you, do not pass by your servant.
Let water now be brought, and let them wash your feet; and refresh yourselves under the tree.
And I will bring bread, and you shall eat; and afterward you shall go on your way, since you have turned aside to your servant.” And they said, “Do as you have said.”
And Abraham hurried to the tent, to Sarah, and said to her, “Hurry, knead three measures of fine flour, and make cakes baked in the embers.”
And Abraham ran to the cattle, and took a tender and good calf, and gave it to the servant; and he hurried to prepare it.
And he took curds, and milk, and the calf he had prepared, and set them before them; and they ate. And he stood beside them under the tree.
And he said to him, “Where is Sarah your wife?” And he answered and said, “There, in the tent.”
And he said, “I will surely return to you at this season, when the time comes round; and Sarah your wife shall have a son.” And Sarah heard at the door of the tent, being behind him.
Now Abraham and Sarah were old, advanced in days; and the way of women had ceased with Sarah.
And Sarah laughed within herself, saying, “It has not happened to me until now, and my lord is old.”
And the Lord said to Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh within herself, saying, ‘Shall I indeed bear a child, though I have grown old?’
Is any word impossible with God? At this season I will return to you, when the time comes round; and Sarah shall have a son.”
And Sarah denied it, saying, “I did not laugh”; for she was afraid. And He said, “No, but you did laugh.”
And the men rose from there and looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah; and Abraham went with them to escort them on their way.
And the Lord said, “Shall I hide from Abraham My servant what I am doing?
Abraham shall surely become a great and numerous nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him.

For I knew that he would command his sons and his household after him; and they shall keep the ways of the Lord, to do righteousness and judgment, that the Lord may bring upon Abraham all that He has spoken to him.”
And the Lord said, “The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah has increased, and their sins are exceedingly great.
So I will go down and see whether they are being brought to an end according to their cry which comes to Me; and if not, that I may know.”
And the men turned from there and came to Sodom; but Abraham stood before the Lord.
And Abraham drew near and said, “Wilt Thou destroy the righteous with the ungodly, and shall the righteous be as the ungodly?
If there are fifty righteous in the city, wilt Thou destroy them? Wilt Thou not spare the whole place for the sake of the fifty righteous, if they are there?
By no means shalt Thou do such a thing, to kill the righteous with the ungodly, so that the righteous shall be as the ungodly. By no means! Thou who judgest all the earth, wilt Thou not do justice?”
And the Lord said, “If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, I will spare the whole place for their sake.”
And Abraham answered and said, “Now I have begun to speak to the Lord, though I am earth and ashes.
If the fifty righteous lack five, wilt Thou destroy the whole city for the five?” And He said, “I will surely not destroy it if I find forty-five there.”
And he spoke to Him yet again and said, “What if forty are found there?” And He said, “I will surely not destroy it for the sake of the forty.”
And he said, “I pray Thee, Lord, allow me to speak: what if thirty are found there?” And He said, “I will surely not destroy it if I find thirty there.”
And he said, “Since I may speak to the Lord, what if twenty are found there?” And He said, “I will surely not destroy it for the sake of the twenty.”
And he said, “I pray Thee, Lord, allow me to speak once more: what if ten are found there?” And He said, “I will surely not destroy it for the sake of the ten.”
And the Lord departed when He had finished speaking to Abraham; and Abraham returned to his place.
And the two angels came to Sodom at evening; and Lot sat beside the gate of Sodom. And when Lot saw them, he rose up to meet them, and bowed his face to the earth,

and said, “Behold, my lords, turn aside into your servant’s house, and lodge there, and wash your feet; and you shall rise early and go on your way.” And they said, “No; but we will lodge in the square.”
And he urged them greatly; and they turned aside to him, and entered into his house. And he made them a feast with drink, and baked unleavened bread for them; and they ate.
Before they lay down, the men of the city, the Sodomites, surrounded the house, from young to old, all the people together.
And they called Lot out, and said to him, “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, that we may lie with them.”
And Lot went out to them at the entrance, and shut the door behind him.
And he said to them, “By no means, brothers; do not act wickedly.

I have two daughters who have not known a man; I will bring them out to you, and do with them as you please. Only do nothing unjust to these men, for they have come under the shelter of my roof beams.”

And they said, “Stand back there. You came alone to live as a stranger; will you also pass judgment? So now we will afflict you more than them.” And they pressed hard upon the man, Lot, and drew near to break the door.
But the men stretched out their hands, and drew Lot to them into the house, and shut the door of the house.
And they struck the men who were at the door of the house with blindness, from small to great; and they became helpless in seeking the door.
And the men said to Lot, “Do you have anyone here, sons-in-law, or sons, or daughters? Or if you have anyone else in the city, bring them out of this place.
For we will destroy this place, because their cry has risen before the Lord; and the Lord has sent us to blot it out.”

And Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who had taken his daughters, and said, “Arise, and depart from this place; for the Lord will blot out the city.” But he seemed to his sons-in-law like someone joking.
And at dawn, the angels urged Lot, saying, “Arise, take your wife and your two daughters whom you have, and depart, so that you do not perish with the lawless deeds of the city.”
And they were troubled; and the angels took hold of his hand, and the hand of his wife, and the hands of his two daughters, because the Lord spared him.

And when they had brought them outside, they said, “Save your own life. Do not look behind you or stand anywhere in the surrounding country. Escape to the mountain, so that you are not swept away with them.”
And Lot said to them, “I beg you, lord,
for your servant has found mercy before you, and you have shown me your great righteousness by preserving my life. Yet I cannot escape to the mountain, for calamities may overtake me, and I may die.
Behold, this city is near enough for me to flee to, and it is small. There I shall be saved; is it not small? And my soul shall live.”
And he said to him, “Behold, I have regarded your face in this matter also, that I will not overthrow the city of which you have spoken.
So hurry and be saved there; for I can do nothing until you enter it.” Therefore he called the name of that city Zoar.
The sun rose upon the earth, and Lot entered into Zoar.
And the Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrah sulphur and fire from the Lord out of the heaven;
and He overthrew those cities, and all the surrounding country, and all that lived in the cities, and all that sprang from the earth.
And his wife looked behind her, and became a pillar of salt.
And Abraham rose early in the morning, and went to the place where he had stood before the Lord.
And he looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and toward the land of the surrounding country; and he saw, and behold, a flame rose from the earth as the vapour of a furnace.
And when the Lord blotted out all the cities of the surrounding country, God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out from the midst of the overthrow, when the Lord overthrew the cities where Lot lived.
And Lot went up out of Zoar, and lived in the mountain, and his two daughters with him; for he was afraid to live in Zoar. And he lived in the cave, he and his two daughters with him.
And the older said to the younger, “Our father is old, and there is no man upon the earth to come in to us as is the way of all the earth.
Come, let us give our father wine to drink, and lie with him, and raise up seed from our father.”
And they gave their father wine to drink that night; and the older went in and lay with her father that night. And he did not know when she lay down, nor when she arose.

And the next day the older daughter said to the younger, “Behold, I lay with our father yesterday. Let us give him wine to drink tonight also; and go in and lie with him, and let us raise up seed from our father.”
And they gave their father wine to drink that night also; and the younger went in and lay with her father. And he did not know when she lay down, nor when she arose.
And both the daughters of Lot conceived by their father.
And the older daughter bore a son, and called his name Moab, saying, “From my father.” He is the father of the Moabites to this day.
And the younger daughter also bore a son, and called his name Amman, “Son of my kindred.” He is the father of the Ammanites to this day.
And Abraham journeyed from there to the land toward the south, and lived between Kadesh and Shur, and lived as a stranger in Gerar.

And Abraham said concerning Sarah his wife, “She is my sister”; for he feared to say, “She is my wife,” lest the men of the city should slay him for her sake. And Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took Sarah.
And God came to Abimelech in his sleep by night, and said, “Behold, you are to die because of the woman whom you have taken; for she is married to a husband.”
But Abimelech had not touched her; and he said, “Lord, wilt Thou destroy a nation that is ignorant and righteous?
Did he not say to me, ‘She is my sister’? And she herself said to me, ‘He is my brother.’ I have done this with a pure heart and with righteousness of hands.”
And God said to him in his sleep, “I also knew that you did this with a pure heart; and I spared you, that you would not sin against Me. Therefore I did not allow you to touch her.
Now therefore return the wife to the man, for he is a prophet; and he shall pray for you, and you shall live. But if you do not return her, know that you shall die, you and all that is yours.”
And Abimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and spoke all these words in their ears; and all the men were very afraid.

And Abimelech called Abraham, and said to him, “What is this that you have done to us? Have we sinned against you, that you have brought upon me and upon my kingdom a great sin? You have done to me a deed which no man would do.”
And Abimelech said to Abraham, “What did you see, that you did this thing?”
And Abraham said, “For I said, ‘Surely there is no reverence for God in this place; and they will slay me for my wife’s sake.’
And indeed she is my sister by my father, but not by my mother; and she became my wife.
And when God brought me out from my father’s house, I said to her, ‘You shall show me this righteousness: in every place where we come, say of me, “He is my brother.”’”
And Abimelech took a thousand didrachms, and sheep, and calves, and male slaves, and female slaves, and gave them to Abraham; and he restored to him Sarah his wife.
And Abimelech said to Abraham, “Behold, my land is before you; live wherever you please.”
And to Sarah he said, “Behold, I have given your brother a thousand didrachms. These shall be for the honour of your face, and for all the women with you; and in all things speak the truth.”
And Abraham prayed to God; and God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his slave women, and they bore children.
For the Lord had wholly shut every womb from outside in the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.
And the Lord visited Sarah as He had said, and the Lord did to Sarah as He had spoken.
And Sarah conceived, and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the season of which the Lord had spoken to him.
And Abraham called the name of his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.
And Abraham circumcised Isaac on the eighth day, as God had commanded him.
Now Abraham was a hundred years old when Isaac his son was born to him.
And Sarah said, “The Lord has made laughter for me; for whoever hears shall rejoice with me.”
And she said, “Who shall tell Abraham that Sarah is nursing a child? For I have borne a son in my old age.”
And the child grew, and was weaned; and Abraham made a great feast on the day that Isaac his son was weaned.
And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, who was born to Abraham, playing with Isaac her son.
And she said to Abraham, “Cast out this slave woman and her son; for the son of this slave woman shall not inherit with my son Isaac.”
And the saying seemed exceedingly harsh in Abraham’s sight, concerning his son.

And God said to Abraham, “Do not let the saying be harsh in your sight concerning the child and the slave woman. In all that Sarah says to you, listen to her voice; for in Isaac seed shall be called to you.
And I will also make the son of this slave woman a great nation, for he is your seed.”

And Abraham rose in the morning, and took loaves and a skin of water, and gave them to Hagar, and laid them upon her shoulder, and the child also, and sent her away. And she departed, and wandered in the wilderness near the Well of the Oath.
And the water in the skin ran out; and she cast the child beneath a fir tree.
And she went and sat opposite him, far off, about a bowshot; for she said, “I will not see the death of my child.” And she sat opposite him; and the child cried aloud and wept.

And God heard the voice of the child from the place where he was; and an angel of God called to Hagar out of the heaven, and said to her, “What is wrong, Hagar? Do not fear; for God has heard the voice of your child from the place where he is.
Arise, take the child, and hold him with your hand; for I will make him a great nation.”
And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of living water; and she went, and filled the skin with water, and gave the child to drink.
And God was with the child, and he grew, and lived in the wilderness, and became an archer.
And he lived in the wilderness of Paran; and his mother took him a wife from the land of Egypt.
And at that time Abimelech, and Ahuzzath his groomsman, and Phicol the chief commander of his army, spoke to Abraham, saying, “God is with you in all that you do.

Now therefore swear to me by God that you will not wrong me, nor my seed, nor my name; but according to the righteousness which I have shown to you, you shall deal with me, and with the land where you have lived as a stranger.”
And Abraham said, “I will swear.”
And Abraham reproved Abimelech concerning the wells of water which Abimelech’s servants had taken away.
And Abimelech said to him, “I did not know who had done this thing; you did not tell me, nor did I hear of it until today.”
And Abraham took sheep and calves, and gave them to Abimelech; and the two made a covenant.
And Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock apart.
And Abimelech said to Abraham, “What are these seven ewe lambs which you have set apart?”
And Abraham said, “You shall take these seven ewe lambs from my hand, that they may be a witness to me that I have dug this well.”
Therefore he called the name of that place the Well of Swearing, because there they both swore.
And they made a covenant at the Well of the Oath. And Abimelech rose up, and Ahuzzath his groomsman, and Phicol the chief commander of his army; and they returned to the land of the Philistines.
And Abraham planted a field at the Well of the Oath, and there called upon the name of the Lord, the Everlasting God.
And Abraham lived as a stranger in the land of the Philistines many days.
And after these things God tested Abraham, and said to him, “Abraham, Abraham.” And he said, “Behold, here am I.”
And He said, “Take your son, your beloved, whom you have loved, Isaac, and go to the high land; and offer him there for a whole burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I shall tell you.”

And Abraham rose in the morning, and saddled his female donkey, and took with him two servants and Isaac his son. And he split wood for the whole burnt offering, and arose and went, and came to the place of which God had spoken to him.
On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place far off.
And Abraham said to his servants, “Stay here with the female donkey; and I and the lad will go over there, and worship, and return to you.”
And Abraham took the wood of the whole burnt offering, and laid it upon Isaac his son; and he took the fire in his hand, and the knife. And the two went together.
And Isaac spoke to Abraham his father, and said, “Father.” And he said, “What is it, child?” And he said, “Behold the fire and the wood; but where is the sheep for the whole burnt offering?”
And Abraham said, “God will provide for Himself a sheep for the whole burnt offering, child.” And the two went together,

and came to the place of which God had spoken to him. And Abraham built an altar there, and laid the wood upon it, and bound together the feet of Isaac his son, and laid him upon the altar, upon the wood.
And Abraham stretched out his hand to take the knife, to slaughter his son.
And an angel of the Lord called to him out of the heaven, and said to him, “Abraham, Abraham.” And he said, “Behold, here am I.”
And he said, “Do not lay your hand upon the lad or do anything to him; for now I know that you fear God, and have not spared your beloved son for my sake.”

And Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, one ram was caught by its horns in a sabek plant. And Abraham went and took the ram, and offered it for a whole burnt offering instead of Isaac his son.
And Abraham called the name of that place The Lord Has Seen, that they might say today, “In the mountain the Lord appeared.”
And an angel of the Lord called to Abraham a second time out of the heaven,
saying, “By Myself I have sworn, says the Lord: because you have done this thing, and have not spared your beloved son for My sake,
surely I will bless you, and greatly multiply your seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand upon the shore of the sea; and your seed shall inherit the cities of their adversaries.
And in your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed, because you have listened to My voice.”
And Abraham returned to his servants; and they arose and went together to the Well of the Oath. And Abraham lived at the Well of the Oath.
And after these things Abraham was told, “Behold, Milcah also has borne sons to Nahor your brother:
Uz the firstborn, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of the Syrians,
and Chesed, and Azau, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”
And Bethuel begot Rebekah. Milcah bore these eight sons to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
And his concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tabek, and Gaham, and Tochos, and Mocha.
And the life of Sarah was a hundred and twenty-seven years.
And Sarah died in the city of Arbok, which is in the hollow, that is, Hebron, in the land of Canaan; and Abraham came to lament Sarah and to mourn.
And Abraham rose up from his dead, and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying,
“I am a resident foreigner and a sojourner among you. So give me a possession for burial among you, that I may bury my dead away from me.”
And the sons of Heth answered Abraham, saying,
“No, lord; hear us. You are a king from God among us. Bury your dead in the choicest of our tombs; for none of us shall withhold his tomb from you, that you may bury your dead there.”
And Abraham rose up and bowed himself to the people of the land, the sons of Heth.
And Abraham spoke to them, saying, “If it is your will that I bury my dead from before my face, hear me, and speak for me to Ephron the son of Zohar,
that he may give me the double cave which he has, which is in a part of his field. Let him give it to me for its full worth in silver among you for a possession for burial.”
Now Ephron sat among the sons of Heth. And Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the hearing of the sons of Heth, and of all that entered into the city, saying,
“Come to me, lord, and hear me. I give you the field and the cave in it; before all my fellow citizens I have given it to you. Bury your dead.”
And Abraham bowed himself before the people of the land,
and said to Ephron in the ears of the people of the land, “Since you are on my side, hear me. Take the silver of the field from me, and I will bury my dead there.”
And Ephron answered Abraham, saying,
“No, lord; I have heard. Land worth four hundred didrachms of silver, what is that between me and you? Bury your dead.”
And Abraham listened to Ephron; and Abraham paid to Ephron the silver which he had named in the ears of the sons of Heth, four hundred didrachms of silver approved by merchants.
And the field of Ephron at the Double Cave, which is opposite Mamre, the field and the cave in it, and every tree in the field within all its borders all around, was established
to Abraham for a possession, before the sons of Heth and all that entered into the city.
Afterward Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the double cave of the field, opposite Mamre, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan.
And the field and the cave in it were confirmed to Abraham for a possession for burial, from the sons of Heth.
Now Abraham was old, advanced in days; and the Lord had blessed Abraham in all things.
And Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his house, who ruled over all that he had, “Put your hand under my thigh,
and I will make you swear by the Lord, the God of the heaven and the God of the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son Isaac from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell;
but you shall go to my land, where I was born, and to my tribe, and take a wife for my son Isaac from there.”
And the servant said to him, “Perhaps the woman will not be willing to follow me to this land; shall I bring your son back to the land from where you came?”
And Abraham said to him, “Take care not to bring my son back there.

The Lord, the God of the heaven and the God of the earth, who took me from my father’s house and from the land where I was born, who spoke to me and swore to me, saying, ‘I will give this land to you, and to your seed,’ He shall send His angel before you; and you shall take a wife for my son Isaac from there.
But if the woman is not willing to come with you to this land, you shall be free from this oath; only do not bring my son back there.”
And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and swore to him concerning this matter.
And the servant took ten camels from the camels of his master, and some of all his master’s good things with him; and he arose, and went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
And he made the camels lie down outside the city, beside the well of water, toward evening, when the women go forth to draw water.
And he said, “Lord, God of my master Abraham, grant me success today, and show mercy to my master Abraham.
Behold, I stand beside the spring of water, and the daughters of those who live in the city come out to draw water.

And let the virgin to whom I shall say, ‘Lower your water jar, that I may drink,’ and who shall say to me, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels until they cease drinking,’ be the one whom Thou hast prepared for Thy servant Isaac. And by this I shall know that Thou hast shown mercy to my master Abraham.”
And before he had finished speaking in his mind, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, having her water jar upon her shoulder.
Now the maiden was very beautiful to look at; she was a virgin, and no man had known her. And she went down to the spring, and filled her water jar, and came up.
And the servant ran to meet her, and said, “Give me a little water to drink from your water jar.”
And she said, “Drink, my lord.” And she hurried, and lowered her water jar upon her arm, and gave him to drink,
until he ceased drinking. And she said, “I will draw water for your camels also, until they have all drunk.”
And she hurried, and emptied her water jar into the trough, and ran again to the well to draw water; and she drew water for all the camels.
And the man watched her, and remained silent, to know whether the Lord had prospered his journey or not.
And when all the camels had ceased drinking, the man took golden earrings, each a drachma in weight, and two bracelets for her hands, ten gold pieces in weight.
And he asked her, and said, “Whose daughter are you? Tell me, is there room with your father for us to lodge?”
And she said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor.”
And she said to him, “We have both straw and much fodder, and room to lodge.”
And the man was well pleased, and worshipped the Lord,
and said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken His righteousness and truth toward my master. The Lord has prospered my way to the house of my master’s brother.”
And the maiden ran and told her mother’s house of these things.
Now Rebekah had a brother, whose name was Laban; and Laban ran to the man outside, beside the spring.

And when he saw the earrings and the bracelets upon his sister’s hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, “This is what the man said to me,” he came to the man, who stood beside the camels at the spring,
and said to him, “Come in; blessed be the Lord. Why are you standing outside? For I have prepared the house, and a place for the camels.”
And the man entered into the house, and unloaded the camels. And straw and fodder were given to the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men with him.
And loaves were set before them to eat. But he said, “I will not eat until I have spoken my words.” And they said, “Speak.”
And he said, “I am Abraham’s servant.
And the Lord has greatly blessed my master, and he is exalted; and He has given him sheep, and calves, silver and gold, male slaves and female slaves, camels and donkeys.
And Sarah, my master’s wife, bore one son to my master after he was old; and he has given him all that he had.
And my master made me swear, saying, ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I sojourn;
but you shall go to my father’s house, and to my tribe, and take a wife for my son from there.’
And I said to my master, ‘Perhaps the woman will not come with me.’

And he said to me, ‘The Lord, before whom I have been pleasing, He shall send His angel with you, and prosper your journey; and you shall take a wife for my son from my tribe, and from my father’s house.
Then you shall be free from my curse; for when you come to my tribe, if they do not give her to you, you shall be free from my oath.’
And I came today to the spring, and said, ‘Lord, God of my master Abraham, if Thou wilt prosper the journey I am now making,

behold, I stand beside the spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city shall come out to draw water. Let the virgin to whom I shall say, “Give me a little water to drink from your water jar,”

and who shall say to me, “Drink, and I will draw water for your camels also,” be the woman whom the Lord has prepared for His own servant Isaac. And by this I shall know that Thou hast shown mercy to my master Abraham.’

And before I had finished speaking in my mind, immediately Rebekah came out, having her water jar upon her shoulder; and she went down to the spring, and drew water. And I said to her, ‘Give me a drink.’
And she hurried, and lowered her water jar, and said, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels.’ And I drank, and she watered my camels.

And I asked her, and said, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ And she said, ‘I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.’ And I put the earrings upon her, and the bracelets about her hands.

And I was well pleased, and worshipped the Lord, and blessed the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, who had prospered my way in the way of truth, to take the daughter of my master’s brother for his son.
Now therefore, if you will show mercy and righteousness to my master, tell me; and if not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand or to the left.”
And Laban and Bethuel answered and said, “This command has come from the Lord; we cannot therefore oppose you with evil against good.
Behold, Rebekah is before you; take her and depart, and let her be the wife of your master’s son, as the Lord has spoken.”
And when Abraham’s servant heard these words, he bowed to the earth before the Lord.
And the servant brought out articles of silver and gold, and garments, and gave them to Rebekah; and he gave gifts to her brother and her mother.
And they ate and drank, he and the men with him, and slept. And he rose in the morning, and said, “Send me away, that I may go to my master.”
And her brothers and her mother said, “Let the maiden abide with us about ten days, and afterward she shall go.”
And he said to them, “Do not hinder me, since the Lord has prospered my journey; send me away, that I may go to my master.”
And they said, “Let us call the maiden, and ask of her own mouth.”
And they called Rebekah, and said to her, “Will you go with this man?” And she said, “I will go.”
And they sent away Rebekah their sister, and her possessions, and Abraham’s servant, and those who were with him.
And they blessed Rebekah their sister, and said to her, “You are our sister; become thousands of ten thousands, and let your seed inherit the cities of their adversaries.”
And Rebekah arose, and her maidservants, and they mounted the camels, and went with the man; and the servant took Rebekah and departed.
Now Isaac was journeying through the wilderness near the Well of the Vision; and he lived in the land toward the south.
And Isaac went out to meditate in the plain toward evening; and he lifted up his eyes, and saw camels coming.
And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and saw Isaac, and leaped down from the camel,
and said to the servant, “Who is that man walking in the plain to meet us?” And the servant said, “It is my master.” And she took her veil, and covered herself.
And the servant told Isaac all the things which he had done.
And Isaac entered into his mother’s house, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife, and he loved her; and Isaac was comforted concerning Sarah his mother.
And Abraham took another wife, whose name was Keturah.
And she bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
And Jokshan begot Sheba, Teman, and Dedan; and the sons of Dedan were Raguel, Nabdeel, Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
And the sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abira, and Elraga. All these were the sons of Keturah.
And Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac his son.
But to the sons of his concubines Abraham gave gifts, and while he was still alive he sent them away from Isaac his son, eastward into the land of the east.
And these were the years of the days of Abraham’s life which he lived: a hundred and seventy-five years.
And Abraham’s strength failed, and he died in a good old age, an old man and full of days; and he was added to his people.
And Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him in the double cave, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which is opposite Mamre,
the field and the cave which Abraham bought from the sons of Heth. There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife.
And after Abraham died, God blessed Isaac his son; and Isaac lived by the Well of the Vision.
And these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the slave woman of Sarah bore to Abraham.
And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by the names of their generations: Ishmael’s firstborn Nebaioth, and Kedar, Nabdeel, and Massam,
and Mishma, Iduma, and Massa,
and Choddad, Teman, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names in their tents and their dwellings: twelve rulers according to their nations.
And these were the years of Ishmael’s life: a hundred and thirty-seven years. And his strength failed, and he died, and was added to his family.
And he lived from Havilah to Shur, which is opposite Egypt as one goes toward the Assyrians. He lived opposite all his brothers.
And these are the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son: Abraham begot Isaac.
And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian from Mesopotamia, the sister of Laban the Syrian, to be his wife.
And Isaac prayed to the Lord concerning Rebekah his wife, because she was barren; and God heard him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
And the children leaped within her; and she said, “If it is to be this way with me, why is this happening to me?” And she went to inquire of the Lord.
And the Lord said to her, “Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples shall be separated from within you; and one people shall surpass the other, and the greater shall serve the lesser.”
And her days to give birth were fulfilled, and behold, there were twins in her womb.
And the firstborn son came out red, all over like a hairy hide; and he was named Esau.
And afterward his brother came out, and his hand held Esau’s heel; and he was named Jacob. And Isaac was sixty years old when Rebekah bore them.
And the young men grew; and Esau was a man skilled in hunting, a man of the countryside, but Jacob was a man without pretence, dwelling in a house.
And Isaac loved Esau, because his hunting supplied him with food; but Rebekah loved Jacob.
And Jacob cooked a stew; and Esau came from the field, exhausted.
And Esau said to Jacob, “Let me taste some of this red stew, for I am exhausted.” Therefore his name was called Edom.
And Jacob said to Esau, “Sell me your birthright today.”
And Esau said, “Behold, I am going to die; and what use is this birthright to me?”
And Jacob said to him, “Swear to me today.” And he swore to him; and Esau sold his birthright to Jacob.
And Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew; and he ate and drank, and rose and went away. Thus Esau despised his birthright.
And there was a famine in the land, besides the former famine which was in the time of Abraham; and Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
And the Lord appeared to him and said, “Do not go down into Egypt; live in the land that I shall tell you about.
“And live as a stranger in this land, and I will be with you and bless you; for to you and to your seed I will give all this land, and I will establish My oath which I swore to Abraham your father.
“And I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and give to your seed all this land; and in your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed,
“because Abraham your father obeyed My voice, and kept My charges, My commandments, My ordinances, and My statutes.”
And Isaac lived in Gerar.

And the men of the place asked concerning Rebekah his wife, and he said, “She is my sister”; for he feared to say, “She is my wife,” lest the men of the place should kill him because of Rebekah, for she was beautiful to behold.
And he remained there a long time; and Abimelech king of Gerar looked through the window and saw Isaac playing with Rebekah his wife.
And Abimelech called Isaac and said to him, “Surely she is your wife! Why did you say, ‘She is my sister’?” And Isaac said to him, “For I thought, ‘I may die because of her.’”
And Abimelech said to him, “What is this that you have done to us? One of my kin might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought an unwitting offence upon us.”
And Abimelech charged all his people, saying, “Whoever touches this man or his wife shall be liable to death.”
And Isaac sowed in that land, and in that year he reaped barley a hundredfold; and the Lord blessed him.
And the man was exalted, and continued to grow greater, until he became very great.
And he had flocks of sheep, herds of cattle, and much farmland; and the Philistines envied him.
And all the wells which his father’s servants had dug in his father’s time, the Philistines stopped up and filled with earth.
And Abimelech said to Isaac, “Depart from us, for you have become far mightier than we.”
And Isaac departed from there, and camped in the valley of Gerar, and lived there.

And Isaac again dug the wells of water which the servants of Abraham his father had dug, and which the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham his father died; and he called them by the names which Abraham his father had given them.
And Isaac’s servants dug in the valley of Gerar, and found there a well of living water.
And the shepherds of Gerar contended with Isaac’s shepherds, saying that the water was theirs; and he called the name of the well Injustice, for they wronged him.
And Isaac departed from there and dug another well, and they disputed over that also; and he called its name Enmity.

And he departed from there and dug another well, and they did not contend over it; and he called its name Broad Space, saying, “For now the Lord has made room for us, and has increased us in the land.”
And he went up from there to the Well of the Oath.

And the Lord appeared to him that night and said, “I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not fear, for I am with you, and I have blessed you, and will multiply your seed for the sake of Abraham your father.”
And he built an altar there, and called upon the name of the Lord, and pitched his tent there; and Isaac’s servants dug a well there.
And Abimelech came to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath his groomsman, and Phicol the commander of his army.
And Isaac said to them, “Why have you come to me, when you hated me and sent me away from you?”
And they said, “We have clearly seen that the Lord was with you, and we said, ‘Let there be an oath with a curse between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you,
“‘that you shall do us no harm, even as we have not loathed you, and as we have treated you well and sent you away in peace.’ And now you are blessed by the Lord.”
And he made a feast for them, and they ate and drank.
And they rose in the morning and swore one to another; and Isaac sent them away, and they departed from him in safety.
And that same day Isaac’s servants came and told him concerning the well which they had dug, and said, “We found no water.”
And he called it Oath; therefore the name of the city is Well of the Oath to this day.
And Esau was forty years old, and took as wives Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hivite.
And they contended with Isaac and Rebekah.
And when Isaac was old and his eyes were too dim to see, he called Esau his elder son and said to him, “My son.” And he said, “Behold, here am I.”
And he said, “Behold, I have grown old, and do not know the day of my death.
“Now therefore take your gear, your quiver and your bow, and go out into the plain, and hunt game for me.
“And prepare for me savoury food such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat, and that my soul may bless you before I die.”
And Rebekah heard Isaac speaking to Esau his son. And Esau went into the plain to hunt game for his father.
And Rebekah said to Jacob her younger son, “Behold, I heard your father speaking to Esau your brother, saying,
“‘Bring me game, and prepare savoury food for me, that I may eat and bless you before the Lord before I die.’
“Now therefore, my son, listen to me in what I command you.
“Go to the flock, and bring me from there two tender and good young goats; and I will prepare them as savoury food for your father, as he loves.
“And you shall bring it to your father, and he shall eat, that your father may bless you before he dies.”
And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, “Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.
“Perhaps my father will feel me, and I shall be before him as one who treats him with contempt, and shall bring a curse upon myself, and not a blessing.”
And his mother said to him, “Upon me be your curse, my child; only obey my voice, and go and bring them to me.”
And he went and took them, and brought them to his mother; and his mother prepared savoury food, as his father loved.
And Rebekah took the fine clothing of Esau her elder son, which was with her in the house, and clothed Jacob her younger son.
And she put the skins of the young goats upon his arms, and upon the bare parts of his neck.
And she gave the savoury food and the loaves which she had prepared into the hands of Jacob her son.
And he brought them to his father, and said, “Father.” And he said, “Behold, here am I. Who are you, my child?”
And Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Arise, sit, and eat of my game, that your soul may bless me.”
And Isaac said to his son, “How is it that you have found it so quickly, my child?” And he said, “Because the Lord your God put it before me.”
And Isaac said to Jacob, “Draw near to me, that I may feel you, my child, whether you are my son Esau or not.”
And Jacob drew near to Isaac his father; and he felt him and said, “The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are Esau’s hands.”
And he did not recognize him, for his hands were hairy as the hands of Esau his brother; and he blessed him.
And he said, “Are you my son Esau?” And he said, “I am.”
And he said, “Bring it to me, that I may eat of your game, my child, and that my soul may bless you.” And he brought it to him, and he ate; and he brought him wine, and he drank.
And Isaac his father said to him, “Draw near to me, and kiss me, my child.”

And he drew near and kissed him; and he smelled the fragrance of his garments, and blessed him, and said, “Behold, the fragrance of my son is as the fragrance of a full field which the Lord has blessed.
“And may God give you of the dew of heaven, and of the richness of the earth, and abundance of grain and wine.

“Let nations serve you, and rulers shall bow down to you. Be lord over your brother, and your father’s sons shall bow down to you. Cursed be the one who curses you, and blessed be the one who blesses you.”
And when Isaac had finished blessing Jacob his son, and Jacob had gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, Esau his brother came from his hunting.
And he also prepared savoury food, and brought it to his father, and said to his father, “Let my father arise and eat of his son’s game, that your soul may bless me.”
And Isaac his father said to him, “Who are you?” And he said, “I am your firstborn son Esau.”
And Isaac was exceedingly astonished, and said, “Who then hunted game for me and brought it to me? And I ate of all before you came, and blessed him; and let him be blessed.”
And when Esau heard the words of Isaac his father, he cried with a great and exceedingly bitter cry, and said, “Bless me also, father!”
And he said to him, “Your brother came with deceit, and took your blessing.”

And he said, “He was rightly named Jacob, for he has now supplanted me these two times: he took my birthright, and now he has taken my blessing.” And Esau said to his father, “Have you not reserved a blessing for me, father?”
And Isaac answered and said to Esau, “If I have made him your lord, and made all his brothers his household slaves, and sustained him with grain and wine, what shall I do for you, my child?”
And Esau said to his father, “Do you have only one blessing, father? Bless me also, father.” And Isaac was deeply moved; and Esau lifted up his voice and wept.
And Isaac his father answered and said to him, “Behold, your dwelling shall be of the richness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above.
“And you shall live by your sword, and you shall serve your brother; but when you cast down, you shall loosen his yoke from your neck.”

And Esau bore a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him; and Esau said in his mind, “Let the days of mourning for my father draw near, that I may kill Jacob my brother.”
And the words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah; and she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said to him, “Behold, Esau your brother threatens to kill you.
“Now therefore, my child, obey my voice, and arise and flee into Mesopotamia, to Laban my brother at Harran.
“And stay with him a few days, until the fury
“and anger of your brother turn away from you, and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send and bring you back from there, lest I be bereaved of you both in one day.”
And Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of the daughters of the sons of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife from the daughters of this land, why should I live?”
And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, saying, “You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.
“Arise, flee into Mesopotamia, to the house of Bethuel your mother’s father, and take a wife for yourself from there, from the daughters of Laban your mother’s brother.
“And may my God bless you, and increase you, and multiply you; and you shall become assemblies of nations.
“And may He give you the blessing of Abraham my father, to you and to your seed after you, to inherit the land of your sojourning, which God gave to Abraham.”
And Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went into Mesopotamia, to Laban the son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.

And Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and that he had gone into Mesopotamia of Syria to take a wife for himself from there; and that in blessing him he had charged him, saying, “You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan,”
and that Jacob had obeyed his father and his mother, and gone into Mesopotamia of Syria.
And Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan were displeasing in the sight of Isaac his father.
And Esau went to Ishmael, and took Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebaioth, to be his wife in addition to his wives.
And Jacob went out from the Well of the Oath, and went toward Harran.
And he came upon a place and slept there, for the sun had set; and he took one of the stones of the place, and put it by his head, and slept in that place.
And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder was set upon the earth, whose top reached to heaven; and the angels of God ascended and descended upon it.
And the Lord stood firm upon it, and said, “I am the Lord, the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac. Do not fear; the land on which you sleep I will give to you and to your seed.

“And your seed shall be as the sand of the earth, and shall spread toward the sea, and toward the south, and toward the north, and toward the east; and in you and in your seed all the tribes of the earth shall be blessed.
“And behold, I am with you, guarding you on every road wherever you go; and I will bring you back into this land, for I will not forsake you until I have done all that I have spoken to you.”
And Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, “The Lord is in this place, and I did not know it.”
And he was afraid and said, “How fearful is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.”
And Jacob rose in the morning, and took the stone which he had put there by his head, and set it up as a pillar, and poured oil upon its top.
And Jacob called the name of that place House of God; but the name of the city at first was Oulamlous.
And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, “If the Lord God is with me, and guards me on this way that I go, and gives me bread to eat and clothing to wear,
“and brings me back in safety to my father’s house, then the Lord shall be my God.
“And this stone, which I have set up as a pillar, shall be to me a house of God; and of all that Thou givest me I will surely give a tenth to Thee.”
And Jacob lifted up his feet and went into the land of the east, to Laban the son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.
And he looked, and behold, a well in the plain; and three flocks of sheep lay there beside it, for from that well they watered the flocks. And a great stone lay upon the mouth of the well.
And all the flocks were gathered there; and they rolled the stone from the mouth of the well, and watered the sheep, and put the stone back in its place upon the mouth of the well.
And Jacob said to them, “Brothers, where are you from?” And they said, “We are from Harran.”
And he said to them, “Do you know Laban the son of Nahor?” And they said, “We know him.”
And he said to them, “Is he well?” And they said, “He is well.” And behold, Rachel his daughter was coming with the sheep.
And Jacob said, “There is still much of the day left; it is not yet time to gather the livestock. Water the sheep, and go and pasture them.”
And they said, “We cannot, until all the shepherds are gathered, and they roll the stone from the mouth of the well; then we shall water the sheep.”
While he was still speaking to them, Rachel the daughter of Laban came with her father’s sheep, for she tended her father’s sheep.

And when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother’s brother, Jacob drew near and rolled the stone from the mouth of the well, and watered the sheep of Laban his mother’s brother.
And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice and wept.
And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father’s kinsman, and that he was Rebekah’s son; and she ran and told her father these things.
And when Laban heard the name of Jacob his sister’s son, he ran to meet him, and embraced and kissed him, and brought him into his house. And Jacob told Laban all these things.
And Laban said to him, “You are of my bones and of my flesh.” And he remained with him a full month.
And Laban said to Jacob, “Because you are my kinsman, you shall not serve me for nothing. Tell me what your wages shall be.”
And Laban had two daughters: the name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
And Leah’s eyes were weak, but Rachel was beautiful in form and fair to behold.
And Jacob loved Rachel, and said, “I will serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter.”
And Laban said to him, “It is better that I give her to you than that I give her to another man. Stay with me.”
And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they were in his sight as a few days, because he loved her.
And Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in to her.”
And Laban gathered all the men of the place, and made a wedding feast.
And evening came; and Laban took Leah his daughter and brought her to Jacob, and Jacob went in to her.
And Laban gave Zilpah his slave woman to Leah his daughter, to be her slave woman.
And morning came, and behold, it was Leah. And Jacob said to Laban, “What is this that you have done to me? Did I not serve you for Rachel? Why have you deceived me?”
And Laban said, “It is not done this way in our place, to give the younger before the elder.
“Therefore fulfil this one’s week, and I will give you the other also, for another seven years of service that you shall render to me.”
And Jacob did so, and fulfilled her week; and Laban gave him Rachel his daughter to be his wife.
And Laban gave Bilhah his slave woman to Rachel his daughter, to be her slave woman.
And he went in to Rachel; and he loved Rachel more than Leah, and served him another seven years.
And the Lord saw that Leah was hated, and opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.
And Leah conceived and bore Jacob a son; and she called his name Reuben, saying, “For the Lord has seen my humiliation; now my husband will love me.”
And Leah conceived again and bore Jacob a second son, and said, “For the Lord has heard that I am hated, and has given me this one also.” And she called his name Simeon.
And she conceived again and bore a son, and said, “Now my husband will be on my side, for I have borne him three sons.” Therefore she called his name Levi.
And she conceived again and bore a son, and said, “This time I will give thanks to the Lord.” Therefore she called his name Judah; and she ceased bearing.
And Rachel saw that she had borne no children to Jacob, and Rachel envied her sister, and said to Jacob, “Give me children, or I shall die.”
And Jacob was angry with Rachel, and said to her, “Am I in the place of God, who has deprived you of the fruit of the womb?”
And Rachel said to Jacob, “Behold my slave woman Bilhah. Go in to her, and she shall bear upon my knees, that I also may have children through her.”
And she gave him Bilhah her slave woman to be his wife; and Jacob went in to her.
And Bilhah, Rachel’s slave woman, conceived and bore Jacob a son.
And Rachel said, “God has judged in my favour, and has heard my voice, and has given me a son.” Therefore she called his name Dan.
And Bilhah, Rachel’s slave woman, conceived again, and bore Jacob a second son.
And Rachel said, “God has helped me, and I have contended with my sister, and prevailed.” And she called his name Naphtali.
And Leah saw that she had ceased bearing, and took Zilpah her slave woman, and gave her to Jacob to be his wife.
And Jacob went in to her; and Zilpah, Leah’s slave woman, conceived and bore Jacob a son.
And Leah said, “Good fortune!” And she called his name Gad.
And Zilpah, Leah’s slave woman, conceived and bore Jacob another son, the second.
And Leah said, “Blessed am I, for women shall call me blessed.” And she called his name Asher.
And Reuben went out in the days of the wheat harvest, and found mandrake fruit in the field, and brought it to Leah his mother. And Rachel said to Leah, “Give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”

And Leah said, “Is it not enough for you that you have taken my husband? Will you also take my son’s mandrakes?” And Rachel said, “Not so; let him lie with you tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.”
And Jacob came from the field in the evening; and Leah went out to meet him, and said, “You shall come in to me today, for I have hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” And he lay with her that night.
And God heard Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a fifth son.
And Leah said, “God has given me my reward, because I gave my slave woman to my husband.” And she called his name Issachar, which is Reward.
And Leah conceived again, and bore Jacob a sixth son.
And Leah said, “God has given me a good gift; now my husband will choose me, for I have borne him six sons.” And she called his name Zebulun.
And afterward she bore a daughter, and called her name Dinah.
And God remembered Rachel, and God heard her, and opened her womb.
And she conceived and bore Jacob a son. And Rachel said, “God has taken away my reproach.”
And she called his name Joseph, saying, “May God add to me another son.”
And when Rachel had borne Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, “Send me away, that I may go to my own place and to my own land.
“Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served you, that I may depart; for you know the service with which I have served you.”
And Laban said to him, “If I have found grace in your sight, I would divine by signs; for God has blessed me at your coming.
“Name your wages to me, and I will give them.”
And Jacob said to him, “You know how I have served you, and how your livestock have fared with me.
“For you had little before I came, and it has increased to abundance; and the Lord has blessed you wherever I set my foot. And now, when shall I also provide for my own house?”
And Laban said to him, “What shall I give you?” And Jacob said to him, “You shall give me nothing. If you will do this thing for me, I will again tend and guard your flock.
“Let all your flock pass through today, and separate from it every grey animal among the lambs, and every white-marked and spotted animal among the goats; these shall be my wages.
“And my righteousness shall answer for me tomorrow, for my wages are before you. Every goat with me that is not spotted and white-marked, and every lamb that is not grey, shall be counted stolen.”
And Laban said to him, “Let it be according to your word.”

And that day he separated the spotted and white-marked male goats, and all the spotted and white-marked female goats, and everything that had white upon it, and every grey animal among the lambs; and he committed them into the hands of his sons.
And he put a journey of three days between them and Jacob; and Jacob tended Laban’s remaining flock.

And Jacob took fresh rods of styrax, walnut, and plane tree; and Jacob peeled white strips in them, stripping away the green, so that the white which he had peeled appeared in a varied pattern upon the rods.
And he set the rods which he had peeled in the channels of the watering troughs, so that, when the sheep came to drink before the rods, when they came to drink,
the sheep might conceive facing the rods. And the sheep bore young that were white-marked, variously marked, and ash-grey with spots.

And Jacob separated the lambs, and set before the sheep a white-marked ram and every variously marked animal among the lambs; and he set apart flocks for himself, and did not mix them with Laban’s sheep.
And at the time when the sheep were mating and conceiving, Jacob set the rods before the sheep in the troughs, that they might mate facing the rods.
But when the sheep gave birth, he did not set them there. And the unmarked were Laban’s, and the marked were Jacob’s.
And the man became exceedingly, exceedingly wealthy; and he had much livestock, and oxen, and male and female slaves, and camels and donkeys.
And Jacob heard the words of Laban’s sons, saying, “Jacob has taken all that was our father’s, and from that which was our father’s he has made all this glory.”
And Jacob saw Laban’s face, and behold, it was not toward him as before.
And the Lord said to Jacob, “Return to the land of your father and to your kindred, and I will be with you.”
And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah into the field where the flocks were.
And he said to them, “I see your father’s face, that it is not toward me as before; but the God of my father has been with me.
“And you yourselves know that with all my strength I have served your father.
“And your father has cheated me, and changed my wages of ten lambs; but God has not allowed him to harm me.
“If he said, ‘The variously marked shall be your wages,’ then all the sheep bore variously marked young; and if he said, ‘The white shall be your wages,’ then all the sheep bore white young.
“And God has taken away all your father’s livestock, and given them to me.
“And when the sheep were mating, I saw them with my eyes in a dream; and behold, the male goats and rams mounting the sheep and goats were white-marked, variously marked, and ash-grey with spots.
“And the angel of God said to me in a dream, ‘Jacob.’ And I said, ‘What is it?’
“And he said, ‘Lift up your eyes and see the male goats and rams mounting the sheep and goats, white-marked, variously marked, and ash-grey with spots; for I have seen all that Laban does to you.

“‘I am the God who appeared to you in the place of God, where you anointed a pillar to Me, and vowed a vow to Me. Now therefore arise and go out from this land, and depart to the land of your birth, and I will be with you.’”
And Rachel and Leah answered and said to him, “Do we still have any portion or inheritance in our father’s house?
“Are we not counted strangers by him? For he has sold us, and has utterly consumed our money.
“All the wealth and glory which God has taken from our father shall be ours and our children’s. Now therefore do all that God has said to you.”
And Jacob rose, and set his wives and his children upon the camels.
And he led away all his possessions, and all his household goods which he had acquired in Mesopotamia, and all that he had, to go to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan.
And Laban had gone to shear his sheep; and Rachel stole her father’s idols.
And Jacob concealed it from Laban the Syrian, by not telling him that he was fleeing.
And he fled, he and all that he had, and crossed the River, and set out toward the mountain of Gilead.
And on the third day it was told to Laban the Syrian that Jacob had fled.
And he took all his kinsmen with him, and pursued him a journey of seven days, and overtook him in the mountain of Gilead.
And God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream by night, and said to him, “Take care not to speak evil to Jacob.”
And Laban overtook Jacob. And Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain; and Laban stationed his kinsmen in the mountain of Gilead.
And Laban said to Jacob, “What have you done? Why did you flee secretly, and defraud me, and lead away my daughters as captives of the sword?
“If you had told me, I would have sent you away with gladness and music, with tambourines and lyre.
“I was not deemed worthy to kiss my children and my daughters. Now you have acted foolishly.
“And now my hand has power to harm you; but the God of your father said to me yesterday, ‘Take care not to speak evil to Jacob.’
“Now therefore you have gone, for you greatly longed to depart to your father’s house; but why have you stolen my gods?”
And Jacob answered and said to Laban, “For I thought, ‘What if you should take your daughters from me, and all that is mine?’

“Identify what is yours among my possessions, and take it.” And he identified nothing with him. And Jacob said to him, “With whomever you find your gods, he shall not live before our kinsmen.” But Jacob did not know that Rachel his wife had stolen them.

And Laban entered and searched Leah’s dwelling, and found nothing; and he went out from Leah’s dwelling and searched Jacob’s dwelling and the dwelling of the two slave women, and found nothing. And he entered Rachel’s dwelling also.
And Rachel had taken the idols, and put them in the camel’s saddle gear, and sat upon them.

And she said to her father, “Do not take it badly, my lord; I cannot rise before you, for the customary condition of women is upon me.” And Laban searched the whole dwelling, and did not find the idols.
And Jacob was angry, and contended with Laban; and Jacob answered and said to Laban, “What is my offence, and what is my sin, that you have pursued me
“and searched all my belongings? What have you found of all your household goods? Set it here before my kinsmen and your kinsmen, and let them judge between us two.
“These twenty years I have been with you; your sheep and your goats have not miscarried, and I have not eaten the rams of your flock.
“I brought you no animal taken by wild beasts; I myself paid for what was stolen by day and what was stolen by night.
“By day I was consumed by the heat, and by night by the frost; and sleep departed from my eyes.
“These twenty years I have been in your house; I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years among your sheep; and you defrauded me of my wages of ten ewe lambs.
“Unless the God of my father Abraham and the Fear of Isaac had been with me, you would now have sent me away empty. God saw my humiliation and the toil of my hands, and rebuked you yesterday.”

And Laban answered and said to Jacob, “The daughters are my daughters, and the sons are my sons, and the livestock are my livestock; and all that you see is mine and my daughters’. What shall I do today to these women, or to their children whom they have borne?
“Now therefore come, let us make a covenant, I and you, and let it be a witness between me and you.” And he said to him, “Behold, no one is with us; see, God is witness between me and you.”
And Jacob took a stone and set it up as a pillar.

And Jacob said to his kinsmen, “Gather stones.” And they gathered stones and made a heap, and ate and drank there beside the heap. And Laban said to him, “This heap bears witness between me and you today.”
And Laban called it Heap of Witness, but Jacob called it Witness Heap.
