And Laban said to Jacob, “Behold this heap and this pillar which I have set between me and you: this heap bears witness, and this pillar bears witness.” Therefore its name was called The Heap Bears Witness,
and The Watch, because he said, “May God watch between me and you, for we shall be separated one from another.
“If you mistreat my daughters, if you take wives besides my daughters, see, no one is with us.
“For if I do not cross over to you, neither shall you cross this heap and this pillar to me for harm,
“the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor shall judge between us.” And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.
And Jacob offered a sacrifice in the mountain, and called his kinsmen; and they ate and drank, and slept in the mountain.
And Laban rose in the morning, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them; and Laban turned back and departed to his own place.
And Jacob went on his own way; and he lifted up his eyes and saw the camp of God encamped, and the angels of God met him.
And Jacob said when he saw them, “This is the camp of God.” And he called the name of that place Encampments.
And Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother, into the land of Seir, into the country of Edom.
And he charged them, saying, “This is what you shall say to my lord Esau: ‘Thus says your servant Jacob: I have lived as a stranger with Laban, and remained until now.
“‘And I have oxen and donkeys and sheep, and male and female slaves; and I have sent to tell my lord Esau, that your servant may find grace in your sight.’”
And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, “We came to your brother Esau, and behold, he comes to meet you, and four hundred men with him.”
And Jacob was greatly afraid and perplexed; and he divided the people who were with him, and the oxen and the sheep, into two camps.
And Jacob said, “If Esau comes to one camp and strikes it down, the second camp shall escape.”
And Jacob said, “O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, O Lord, who didst say to me, ‘Hurry to the land of your birth, and I will do you good,’
“all the righteousness and all the truth which Thou hast shown to Thy servant suffice for me; for with my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.
“Deliver me from the hand of Esau my brother, for I fear him, lest he come and strike me down, mother with children.
“And Thou didst say, ‘I will surely do you good, and make your seed as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for its multitude.’”
And he slept there that night; and he took gifts from what he had brought, and sent them to Esau his brother:
two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,
thirty nursing camels with their young, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty donkeys and ten foals.
And he committed them into the hands of his servants, each herd apart; and he said to his servants, “Go before me, and leave a space between herd and herd.”
And he charged the first, saying, “If Esau my brother meets you and asks you, saying, ‘Whose are you, and where are you going, and whose are these before you?’
“you shall say, ‘They are your servant Jacob’s. He has sent gifts to my lord Esau, and behold, he himself is behind us.’”
And he charged the first, and the second, and the third, and all who went along behind these flocks, saying, “Speak to Esau in this way when you meet him.

“And you shall say, ‘Behold, your servant Jacob comes behind us.’” For he said, “I will appease him with the gifts going before him, and afterward I shall see his face; for perhaps he will accept me.”
And the gifts passed on before him, but he slept that night in the camp.
And he rose that night, and took his two wives and his two slave women and his eleven children, and crossed the ford of Jabbok.
And he took them and crossed the torrent, and brought over all that he had.
And Jacob was left alone; and a man wrestled with him until morning.
And he saw that he could not prevail against him, and touched the broad part of his thigh; and the broad part of Jacob’s thigh became numb as he wrestled with him.
And he said to him, “Let me go, for dawn has risen.” And he said, “I will not let you go unless you bless me.”
And he said to him, “What is your name?” And he said, “Jacob.”
And he said to him, “Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name, for you have been strong with God, and with men you are mighty.”
And Jacob asked and said, “Tell me your name.” And he said, “Why do you ask my name?” And he blessed him there.
And Jacob called the name of that place Form of God, “For I have seen God face to face, and my life has been preserved.”
And the sun rose upon him as he passed Form of God; and he limped because of his thigh.

Therefore the sons of Israel do not eat the sinew that became numb, which is upon the broad part of the thigh, to this day; for he touched the broad part of Jacob’s thigh, the sinew, and it became numb.
And Jacob lifted up his eyes and saw, and behold, Esau his brother was coming, and four hundred men with him. And Jacob divided the children among Leah and Rachel and the two slave women.
And he put the two slave women and their sons first, and Leah and her children behind, and Rachel and Joseph last.
And he himself went before them, and bowed down to the earth seven times, until he drew near to his brother.
And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced and kissed him, and fell upon his neck; and they both wept.
And he lifted up his eyes and saw the women and the children, and said, “Who are these with you?” And he said, “The children with whom God has shown mercy to your servant.”
And the slave women and their children drew near, and bowed down.
And Leah and her children drew near, and bowed down; and afterward Rachel and Joseph drew near, and bowed down.
And he said, “What do you mean by all these companies which I met?” And he said, “That your servant may find grace in your sight, my lord.”
And Esau said, “I have much, brother; let what is yours be yours.”
And Jacob said, “If I have found grace in your sight, receive the gifts from my hands; for I have seen your face as one might see the face of God, and you will accept me.
“Take my blessings which I have brought to you, for God has shown mercy to me, and I have all things.” And he urged him, and he took them.
And he said, “Let us set out and go straight ahead.”
And he said to him, “My lord knows that the children are tender, and the sheep and cows under my care are nursing; if therefore I drive them hard for one day, all the livestock will die.
“Let my lord go before his servant; and I will make my way slowly, according to the journey before me and the children’s pace, until I come to my lord in Seir.”
And Esau said, “Let me leave with you some of the people who are with me.” And he said, “Why this? It is enough that I have found grace in your sight, my lord.”
And Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.
And Jacob journeyed to Booths, and made houses for himself there, and made booths for his livestock; therefore he called the name of that place Booths.
And Jacob came to Salem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Mesopotamia of Syria; and he camped before the city.
And he bought the portion of the field where he had pitched his tent from Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred lambs.
And he set up an altar there, and called upon the God of Israel.
And Dinah the daughter of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the people of the land.
And Shechem the Horite, son of Hamor and ruler of the land, saw her, and seized her, and lay with her, and violated her.
And he was attached to the soul of Dinah, Jacob’s daughter, and loved the maiden, and spoke to the maiden according to her heart.
And Shechem spoke to Hamor his father, saying, “Take this young woman for me to be my wife.”
And Jacob heard that the son of Hamor had defiled Dinah his daughter; but his sons were with his livestock in the plain, and Jacob kept silence until they came.
And Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to speak with him.

And Jacob’s sons came from the plain; and when they heard, the men were deeply distressed, and were exceedingly grieved, because he had done a disgraceful thing in Israel by lying with Jacob’s daughter; and such a thing must not be.
And Hamor spoke to them, saying, “Shechem my son has set his soul upon your daughter; therefore give her to him to be his wife.
“Intermarry with us; give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for your sons.
“And live among us; behold, the land is broad before you. Live and trade in it, and acquire possessions in it.”
And Shechem said to her father and to her brothers, “Let me find grace in your sight, and whatever you say, we will give.
“Make the marriage payment exceedingly great, and I will give according to whatever you say to me; and give me this young woman to be my wife.”
And Jacob’s sons answered Shechem and Hamor his father with deceit, and spoke to them, because they had defiled Dinah their sister.
And Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, the sons of Leah, said to them, “We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to a man who is uncircumcised; for it is a reproach to us.
“On this condition we will become like you and live among you: if you also become as we are, with every male among you circumcised.
“And we will give our daughters to you, and take wives for ourselves from your daughters; and we will live among you, and be as one family.
“But if you will not listen to us to be circumcised, we will take our daughters and depart.”
And their words pleased Hamor and Shechem the son of Hamor.
And the young man did not delay to do this thing, for he was intent upon Jacob’s daughter; and he was the most honoured of all in his father’s house.
And Hamor and Shechem his son came to the gate of their city, and spoke to the men of their city, saying,
“These men are peaceable with us; let them live in the land and trade in it, for behold, the land is broad before them. We will take their daughters to be our wives, and give our daughters to them.
“Only on this condition will the men become like us, to live with us and be one people: that every male among us be circumcised, even as they are circumcised.
“And shall not their livestock, and their possessions, and their four-footed beasts be ours? Only let us become like them, and they will live with us.”
And all who went out through the gate of their city listened to Hamor and Shechem his son; and they were circumcised in the flesh of their foreskin, every male.
And on the third day, when they were in pain, two of Jacob’s sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword, and entered the city unopposed, and slew every male.
And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah from Shechem’s house, and went out.
And Jacob’s sons came upon the slain, and plundered the city in which they had defiled Dinah their sister.
And they took their sheep and their oxen and their donkeys, whatever was in the city and whatever was in the plain.
And they took captive all their people, and all their household goods, and their wives; and they plundered whatever was in the city and whatever was in the houses.

And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have made me hated, so that I am offensive to all who live in the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites. And I am few in number; and they shall gather against me and cut me down, and I and my household shall be destroyed.”
And they said, “But should they treat our sister as a prostitute?”
And God said to Jacob, “Arise, go up to the place Bethel, and live there; and make an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you were fleeing from the presence of Esau your brother.”
And Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him, “Put away from among you the foreign gods which are with you, and purify yourselves, and change your garments.
“And let us arise and go up to Bethel, and make an altar there to the God who heard me in the day of affliction, who was with me and preserved me on the way which I went.”
And they gave to Jacob the foreign gods which were in their hands, and the earrings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the terebinth in Shechem, and destroyed them to this day.
And Israel departed from Shechem; and the fear of God fell upon the cities around them, and they did not pursue the sons of Israel.
And Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan, which is Bethel, he and all the people who were with him.
And he built an altar there, and called the name of the place Bethel; for there God appeared to him when he was fleeing from the presence of Esau his brother.
And Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died below Bethel under the oak; and Jacob called its name Oak of Mourning.
And God appeared to Jacob again in Luz, when he came from Mesopotamia of Syria; and God blessed him.
And God said to him, “Your name is Jacob; you shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name.”
And God said to him, “I am your God. Increase and multiply; nations and assemblies of nations shall be from you, and kings shall come from your loins.
“And the land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I have given to you; it shall be yours, and I will give this land to your seed after you.”
And God went up from him, from the place where He spoke with him.
And Jacob set up a pillar in the place where He spoke with him, a pillar of stone; and he poured a drink offering upon it, and poured oil upon it.
And Jacob called the name of the place where God spoke with him Bethel.
And Jacob departed from Bethel, and pitched his tent beyond the tower of Gader. And when he drew near to Chabratha, to enter the land of Ephrath, Rachel gave birth, and had hard labour in the birth.
And during her hard labour the midwife said to her, “Take courage, for this also is a son for you.”
And as her soul was departing, for she was dying, she called his name Son of My Sorrow; but his father called him Benjamin.
And Rachel died, and was buried on the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.
And Jacob set up a pillar upon her tomb; this is the pillar of Rachel’s tomb to this day.
And when Israel lived in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father’s concubine; and Israel heard it, and it appeared evil in his sight. And the sons of Jacob were twelve.
The sons of Leah: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
And the sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
And the sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s slave woman: Dan and Naphtali.
And the sons of Zilpah, Leah’s slave woman: Gad and Asher. These are Jacob’s sons, who were born to him in Mesopotamia of Syria.
And Jacob came to Isaac his father at Mamre, to the city of the plain, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan, where Abraham and Isaac lived as strangers.
And the days of Isaac which he lived were a hundred and eighty years.
And his strength failed, and he died, and was added to his family, old and full of days; and Esau and Jacob his sons buried him.
And these are the generations of Esau, who is Edom.
And Esau took wives from the daughters of the Canaanites: Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah the son of Zibeon the Hivite,
and Basemath the daughter of Ishmael, the sister of Nebaioth.
And Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau, and Basemath bore Reuel.
And Oholibamah bore Jeush and Jalam and Korah. These are Esau’s sons who were born to him in the land of Canaan.

And Esau took his wives and his sons and his daughters, and all the persons of his house, and all his possessions and all his livestock, and all that he had acquired and all that he had gained in the land of Canaan; and he went out from the land of Canaan, away from the presence of Jacob his brother.
For their possessions were too great for them to live together, and the land of their sojourning could not support them because of the multitude of their possessions.
And Esau lived in the mountain of Seir; Esau is Edom.
And these are the generations of Esau, the father of Edom, in the mountain of Seir.
And these are the names of Esau’s sons: Eliphaz the son of Adah, Esau’s wife, and Reuel the son of Basemath, Esau’s wife.
And the sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Sophar, Gatam, and Kenaz.
And Timna was the concubine of Eliphaz, Esau’s son, and bore Amalek to Eliphaz. These are the sons of Adah, Esau’s wife.
And these are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the sons of Basemath, Esau’s wife.
And these were the sons of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah the son of Zibeon, Esau’s wife: she bore to Esau Jeush and Jalam and Korah.
These are the chiefs, the sons of Esau. The sons of Eliphaz, Esau’s firstborn: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Sophar, chief Kenaz,
chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek. These are the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Idumea; these are Adah’s sons.
And these are the sons of Reuel, Esau’s son: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah. These are the chiefs of Reuel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basemath, Esau’s wife.
And these are the sons of Oholibamah, Esau’s wife: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, chief Korah. These are the chiefs of Oholibamah.
These are Esau’s sons, and these are their chiefs. These are the sons of Edom.
And these are the sons of Seir the Horite, who lived in the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
and Dishon, Asar, and Rison. These are the chiefs of the Horite, the son of Seir, in the land of Edom.
And Lotan’s sons were Hori and Aiman; and Lotan’s sister was Timna.
And these are Shobal’s sons: Golon, Manahath, Gaibel, Soph, and Oman.
And these are Zibeon’s sons: Aiah and Onan. This is the Onas who found Iamin in the wilderness when he was tending the beasts of burden of Zibeon his father.
And these are Anah’s children: Dishon, and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah.
And these are Dishon’s sons: Amada, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
And these are Asar’s sons: Balaan, Zoukam, Ioukam, and Oukan.
And these are Rison’s sons: Uz and Aram.
These are the chiefs of the Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,
chief Dishon, chief Asar, chief Rison. These are the chiefs of the Horites according to their chiefdoms in the land of Edom.
And these are the kings who reigned in Edom before a king reigned in Israel.
And Balak the son of Beor reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Dennaba.
And Balak died, and Jobab the son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned in his place.
And Jobab died, and Asom from the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
And Asom died, and Hadad the son of Barad, who struck down Midian in the plain of Moab, reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Geththaim.
And Hadad died, and Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place.
And Samlah died, and Shaul from Rehoboth by the River reigned in his place.
And Shaul died, and Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his place.

And Baal-hanan the son of Achbor died, and Arad the son of Barad reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Phogor, and his wife’s name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred the son of Me-zahab.
These are the names of Esau’s chiefs according to their tribes, according to their place, in their regions and in their nations: chief Timna, chief Gola, chief Jether,
chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mazar,
chief Megediel, chief Zaphoim. These are the chiefs of Edom according to their settlements in the land of their possession. This is Esau, the father of Edom.
And Jacob lived in the land where his father had lived as a stranger, in the land of Canaan.

And these are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was tending the sheep with his brothers, a youth among the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father’s wives; and Joseph brought an evil report to Israel their father.
And Jacob loved Joseph more than all his sons, for he was to him a son of his old age; and he made him a tunic of many colours.
And his brothers saw that their father loved him above all his sons, and hated him, and could speak nothing peaceable to him.
And Joseph dreamed a dream, and told it to his brothers.
And he said to them, “Hear this dream which I have dreamed.
“I dreamed that we were binding sheaves in the midst of the plain; and my sheaf arose and stood upright, and your sheaves turned about and bowed down to my sheaf.”
And his brothers said to him, “Shall you indeed reign over us, or shall you indeed have dominion over us?” And they hated him still more because of his dreams and because of his words.
And he saw another dream, and told it to his father and to his brothers, and said, “Behold, I have dreamed another dream, as though the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”
And his father rebuked him, and said to him, “What is this dream which you have dreamed? Shall I and your mother and your brothers indeed come to bow down to you to the earth?”
And his brothers envied him, but his father kept the saying in mind.
And his brothers went to pasture their father’s sheep in Shechem.
And Israel said to Joseph, “Do not your brothers tend the flock in Shechem? Come, I will send you to them.” And he said to him, “Behold, here am I.”
And Israel said to him, “Go and see whether your brothers and the sheep are well, and tell me.” And he sent him from the valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
And a man found him wandering in the plain; and the man asked him, saying, “What are you looking for?”
And he said, “I am looking for my brothers; tell me where they pasture the flock.”
And the man said to him, “They have departed from here, for I heard them saying, ‘Let us go to Dothan.’” And Joseph went after his brothers, and found them in Dothan.
And they saw him far off, before he drew near to them, and plotted wickedly to kill him.
And they said one to another, “Behold, that dreamer comes.
“Now therefore come, let us kill him and cast him into one of the pits, and we will say, ‘An evil beast has devoured him’; and we shall see what shall become of his dreams.”
And Reuben heard, and delivered him from their hands, and said, “Let us not take his life.”
And Reuben said to them, “Shed no blood; cast him into this pit in the wilderness, but lay no hand upon him,” that he might deliver him from their hands and restore him to his father.
And when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped Joseph of the tunic of many colours which was upon him.
And they took him and cast him into the pit; and the pit was empty, having no water.

And they sat down to eat bread; and they lifted up their eyes and saw, and behold, Ishmaelite travellers were coming from Gilead, and their camels were laden with spices and resin and stacte; and they were going to take them down into Egypt.
And Judah said to his brothers, “What profit is there if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?
“Come, let us sell him to these Ishmaelites, and do not let our hands be upon him, for he is our brother and our flesh.” And his brothers listened.
And Midianite merchants passed by; and they drew Joseph up and brought him out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of gold, and brought Joseph down into Egypt.
And Reuben returned to the pit, and did not see Joseph in the pit; and he tore his garments.
And he returned to his brothers and said, “The child is not here; and I, where shall I now go?”
And they took Joseph’s tunic, and slaughtered a young goat, and stained the tunic with the blood.
And they sent the tunic of many colours, and brought it to their father, and said, “We have found this. See whether it is your son’s tunic or not.”
And he recognized it, and said, “It is my son’s tunic; an evil beast has devoured him, a beast has snatched Joseph away.”
And Jacob tore his garments, and put sackcloth upon his loins, and mourned his son many days.
And all his sons and daughters gathered and came to comfort him, but he would not be comforted, saying, “I will go down to my son mourning, into Hades.” And his father wept for him.
And the Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, Pharaoh’s eunuch, the chief cook.
And at that time Judah went down from his brothers, and came to a certain Adullamite man whose name was Hirah.
And Judah saw there a Canaanite man’s daughter named Shua; and he took her, and went in to her.
And she conceived and bore a son, and called his name Er.
And she conceived again and bore a son, and called his name Onan.
And she bore another son, and called his name Shelah. And she was in Chasbi when she bore them.
And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name was Tamar.
And Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil before the Lord, and God put him to death.
And Judah said to Onan, “Go in to your brother’s wife, and perform a brother-in-law’s duty to her, and raise up seed to your brother.”
And Onan knew that the seed would not be his; and whenever he went in to his brother’s wife, he spilled his seed upon the ground, that he might not give seed to his brother.
And it appeared evil before God that he did this, and He put him also to death.

And Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, “Remain a widow in your father’s house until Shelah my son is grown”; for he said, “What if this one also should die, as his brothers?” And Tamar went and lived in her father’s house.
And many days passed, and Shua, Judah’s wife, died; and Judah was comforted, and went up to those who sheared his sheep, he and Hirah his shepherd, the Adullamite, to Timnah.
And it was told to Tamar his daughter-in-law, saying, “Behold, your father-in-law goes up to Timnah to shear his sheep.”

And she took off the garments of her widowhood, and wrapped herself in a veil, and adorned herself, and sat by the gates of Ainan, which is beside the road to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah was grown, but he had not given her to him to be his wife.
And Judah saw her, and thought her to be a prostitute; for she had covered her face, and he did not recognize her.

And he turned aside from the way to her, and said to her, “Allow me to come in to you”; for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, “What will you give me if you come in to me?”
And he said, “I will send you a young goat from the flock.” And she said, “If you will give a pledge until you send it.”
And he said, “What pledge shall I give you?” And she said, “Your ring, and your necklace, and the staff in your hand.” And he gave them to her, and went in to her, and she conceived by him.
And she rose and went away, and took off her veil, and put on the garments of her widowhood.
And Judah sent the young goat by the hand of his shepherd, the Adullamite, to recover the pledge from the woman; and he did not find her.
And he asked the men of the place, “Where is the prostitute who was in Ainan by the way?” And they said, “There was no prostitute here.”
And he returned to Judah, and said, “I did not find her; and the men of the place say there is no prostitute here.”
And Judah said, “Let her keep them, lest we be mocked. I have sent this young goat, but you have not found her.”

And after three months Judah was told, “Tamar your daughter-in-law has acted as a prostitute, and behold, she is with child through her prostitution.” And Judah said, “Bring her out, and let her be burned.”

And as she was being brought out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, “I am with child by the man to whom these belong.” And she said, “See to whom this ring, and this necklace, and this staff belong.”
And Judah recognized them, and said, “Tamar is more in the right than I, because I did not give her to Shelah my son.” And he knew her no more.
And when she gave birth, behold, there were twins in her womb.
And as she was giving birth, one put out his hand; and the midwife took it and bound a scarlet thread upon his hand, saying, “This one shall come out first.”
But as he drew back his hand, immediately his brother came out; and she said, “Why has a barrier been broken through because of you?” And his name was called Perez.
And afterward his brother came out, upon whose hand was the scarlet thread; and his name was called Zerah.
And Joseph was brought down into Egypt; and Potiphar, Pharaoh’s eunuch, the chief cook, an Egyptian man, bought him from the hands of the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.
And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his Egyptian master.
And his master knew that the Lord was with him, and that whatever he did, the Lord made it prosper in his hands.
And Joseph found grace before his master, and pleased him; and he set him over his house, and committed all that he had into Joseph’s hand.

And after he was set over his house and over all that he had, the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of the Lord was upon all that he had, in the house and in the field.
And he committed all that he had into Joseph’s hands, and concerned himself with nothing except the bread which he ate. And Joseph was handsome in form, and very beautiful to look at.
And after these things his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph, and said, “Lie with me.”
But he would not, and said to his master’s wife, “If my master concerns himself with nothing in his house because of me, and has committed all that he has into my hands,
“and nothing in this house is above me, and nothing has been withheld from me except you, because you are his wife, how shall I do this evil thing, and sin before God?”
And though she spoke to Joseph day after day, he did not listen to her, to sleep with her and have relations with her.
And on a certain day Joseph entered the house to do his work, and none of the household was inside.
And she caught him by his garments, saying, “Lie with me.” And he left his garments in her hands, and fled and went outside.
And when she saw that he had left his garments in her hands, and had fled and gone outside,
she called those of the household, and said to them, “See, he has brought us a Hebrew servant to mock us. He came in to me, saying, ‘Lie with me’; and I cried with a loud voice.
“And when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garments beside me, and fled and went outside.”
And she kept his garments beside her until his master came to his house.
And she spoke to him in this way, saying, “The Hebrew servant whom you have brought to us came in to me to mock me, and said to me, ‘I will lie with you.’
“And when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garments beside me, and fled and went outside.”
And when his master heard the words of his wife which she spoke to him, saying, “This is what your servant did to me,” his anger was kindled.
And Joseph’s master took him and cast him into the fortress, into the place where the king’s prisoners were held in the fortress.
And the Lord was with Joseph, and poured mercy upon him, and gave him grace before the chief jailer.
And the chief jailer committed the prison into Joseph’s hand, and all those confined in the prison, and all that they did there.
And the chief jailer concerned himself with nothing because of him; for all was in Joseph’s hand, because the Lord was with him, and whatever he did, the Lord made it prosper in his hands.
And after these things the chief cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the chief baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.
And Pharaoh was angry with his two eunuchs, with the chief cupbearer and with the chief baker.
And he put them in custody with the jailer, in the prison, in the place where Joseph had been taken.
And the chief jailer committed them to Joseph, and he attended them; and they were in custody for some days.
And both dreamed a dream, each his own dream; in that one night each had the vision of his dream: the chief cupbearer and the chief baker of the king of Egypt, who were in the prison.
And Joseph came to them in the morning, and saw them, and they were troubled.
And he asked Pharaoh’s eunuchs who were with him in custody in his master’s house, saying, “Why are your faces downcast today?”
And they said to him, “We have dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it.” And Joseph said to them, “Does not their explanation come through God? Tell me therefore.”
And the chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph, and said, “In my dream there was a vine before me.
“And upon the vine were three branches; and it was flourishing and had put forth shoots, and its clusters of grapes were ripe.
“And Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes and pressed them into the cup, and gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hands.”
And Joseph said to him, “This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.

“In three more days Pharaoh shall remember your office, and restore you to your office as chief cupbearer; and you shall give Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, according to your former office when you were his cupbearer.
“But remember me yourself when it goes well with you, and show mercy to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this fortress.
“For I was indeed stolen from the land of the Hebrews; and here I have done nothing, yet they have cast me into this pit.”
And the chief baker saw that he had interpreted rightly, and said to Joseph, “I also dreamed a dream, and thought I was carrying three baskets of coarse bread upon my head.
“And in the uppermost basket were all kinds of food which King Pharaoh eats, the work of a baker; and the birds of heaven ate them from the basket upon my head.”
And Joseph answered and said to him, “This is its interpretation: the three baskets are three days.
“In three more days Pharaoh shall take your head from you, and hang you upon a tree; and the birds of heaven shall eat your flesh from you.”

And on the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he made a drinking feast for all his servants; and he remembered the office of the chief cupbearer and the office of the chief baker among his servants.
And he restored the chief cupbearer to his office, and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.
But the chief baker he hanged, as Joseph had interpreted to them.
But the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.
And after two full years Pharaoh dreamed a dream. He thought he was standing beside the river.
And behold, as though from the river there came up seven cows, fair in appearance and choice in flesh, and they grazed among the reeds.
And seven other cows came up after them from the river, ugly in appearance and lean in flesh, and they grazed beside the cows upon the riverbank.
And the seven cows which were ugly and lean in flesh devoured the seven cows which were fair in appearance and choice. And Pharaoh awoke.
And he dreamed a second time, and behold, seven ears of grain came up upon one stalk, choice and good.
And seven other ears sprouted after them, thin and blighted by the wind.
And the seven thin ears, blighted by the wind, swallowed the seven choice and full ears. And Pharaoh awoke, and it was a dream.
And morning came, and his soul was troubled; and he sent and called all the interpreters of Egypt and all its wise men. And Pharaoh told them the dream, and there was none to explain it to Pharaoh.
And the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, “I remember my offence today.
“Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and put us in custody in the house of the chief cook, me and the chief baker.
“And we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he; each of us saw his own dream.
“And a young Hebrew servant of the chief cook was with us, and we told him, and he interpreted to us.
“And as he interpreted to us, so it happened: I was restored to my office, and he was hanged.”
And Pharaoh sent and called Joseph; and they brought him out of the fortress, and shaved him, and changed his garments; and he came to Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have dreamed a dream, and there is none to interpret it; but I have heard it said concerning you, that when you hear dreams, you can interpret them.”
And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, “Without God, no answer bringing deliverance shall be given to Pharaoh.”
And Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, “In my dream I thought I was standing beside the bank of the river.
“And as though from the river there came up seven cows, fair in appearance and choice in flesh, and they grazed among the reeds.
“And behold, seven other cows came up after them from the river, wretched and ugly in appearance and lean in flesh; I have never seen such ugly cows in all the land of Egypt.
“And the seven ugly and lean cows devoured the first seven cows, which were fair and choice.
“And they entered into their bellies, yet it could not be perceived that they had entered into their bellies; and their appearance was ugly as at first. And I awoke, and slept again.
“And I saw again in my dream, and as though seven ears of grain came up upon one stalk, full and good.
“And seven other ears sprouted beside them, thin and blighted by the wind.
“And the seven thin ears, blighted by the wind, swallowed the seven good and full ears. I told the interpreters, but there was none to explain it to me.”
And Joseph said to Pharaoh, “Pharaoh’s dream is one. God has shown to Pharaoh what He is about to do.
“The seven fair cows are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years. Pharaoh’s dream is one.
“And the seven lean cows which came up after them are seven years; and the seven thin ears, blighted by the wind, shall be seven years of famine.
“And this is the word which I have spoken to Pharaoh: God has shown to Pharaoh what He is about to do.
“Behold, seven years of great abundance are coming in all the land of Egypt.
“And seven years of famine shall come after them, and they shall forget the plenty in all the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land.
“And the abundance shall not be known in the land because of the famine which shall follow, for it shall be exceedingly severe.
“And as for Pharaoh’s dream being repeated twice, it is because the word from God shall be true, and God shall hasten to do it.
“Now therefore seek out a prudent and discerning man, and set him over the land of Egypt.
“And let Pharaoh act, and appoint governors over the land; and let them take a fifth of all the produce of the land of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.
“And let them gather all the food of these seven good years which are coming; and let the grain be gathered under Pharaoh’s hand, and let food be kept in the cities.
“And the food shall be kept for the land against the seven years of famine which shall be in the land of Egypt, and the land shall not be destroyed by the famine.”
And the words pleased Pharaoh and all his servants.
And Pharaoh said to all his servants, “Shall we find such a man as this, who has the Spirit of God in him?”
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since God has shown you all these things, there is no man more prudent and discerning than you.
“You shall be over my house, and all my people shall obey your mouth; only in the throne shall I be above you.”
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Behold, I set you today over all the land of Egypt.”
And Pharaoh took his ring from his hand and put it upon Joseph’s hand, and clothed him in a robe of fine linen, and put a golden collar about his neck.
And he made him ride in his second chariot, and a herald proclaimed before him; and he set him over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh; without you no one shall lift up his hand in all the land of Egypt.”
And Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Psonthomphanech; and he gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, to be his wife.
And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from Pharaoh’s presence, and passed through all the land of Egypt.
And the land brought forth sheaves during the seven years of abundance.
And he gathered all the food of the seven years in which there was abundance in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities; the food from the plains around each city he laid up within it.
And Joseph gathered grain like the sand of the sea, in great abundance, until they could not count it, for it was beyond counting.
And to Joseph were born two sons before the seven years of famine came, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, bore to him.
And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, “For God has made me forget all my toil, and all the affairs of my father.”
And the name of the second he called Ephraim, “For God has increased me in the land of my humiliation.”
And the seven years of abundance which were in the land of Egypt passed away.
And the seven years of famine began to come, as Joseph had said; and there was famine in all the land, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
And all the land of Egypt hungered, and the people cried to Pharaoh for bread. And Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph; do whatever he says to you.”
And the famine was upon the face of all the earth; and Joseph opened all the granaries, and sold to all the Egyptians.
And all the countries came into Egypt to buy from Joseph, for the famine prevailed in all the earth.
And Jacob saw that there was grain for sale in Egypt, and said to his sons, “Why are you idle?
“Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy us a little food, that we may live and not die.”
And Joseph’s ten brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
But he did not send Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, with his brothers; for he said, “What if sickness should befall him?”
And the sons of Israel came to buy among those who came, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
And Joseph was ruler of the land; he was the one who sold to all the people of the land. And Joseph’s brothers came and bowed down before him, with their faces to the earth.

And Joseph saw his brothers and recognized them, but made himself a stranger to them, and spoke harshly to them, and said to them, “Where have you come from?” And they said, “From the land of Canaan, to buy food.”
And Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.
And Joseph remembered the dreams which he had seen, and said to them, “You are spies; you have come to inspect the tracks of the country.”
And they said, “No, my lord; your servants have come to buy food.
“We are all sons of one man; we are peaceable men, and your servants are no spies.”
And he said to them, “No, but you have come to see the tracks of the land.”
And they said, “Your servants are twelve brothers in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is with our father today, and the other is no more.”
And Joseph said to them, “This is what I said to you, saying, ‘You are spies.’
“By this you shall be revealed: by the health of Pharaoh, you shall not go out from here unless your youngest brother comes here.

“Send one of you and bring your brother, but you shall be taken into custody until your words are made clear, whether you speak truth or not; and if not, by the health of Pharaoh, surely you are spies.”
And he put them in custody for three days.
And on the third day he said to them, “Do this, and you shall live, for I fear God.
“If you are peaceable men, let one of your brothers be held in custody; but you go, and carry away the grain which you have bought for your provision.
“And bring your youngest brother to me, and your words shall be believed; but if not, you shall die.” And they did so.

And they said one to another, “Yes, we are in sin concerning our brother, for we disregarded the affliction of his soul when he begged us, and did not listen to him. Therefore this affliction has come upon us.”
And Reuben answered and said to them, “Did I not speak to you, saying, ‘Do not wrong the child’? And you did not listen to me; and behold, his blood is required.”
But they did not know that Joseph understood, for the interpreter was between them.
And Joseph turned away from them and wept. And he came to them again, and spoke to them, and took Simeon from among them, and bound him before them.
And Joseph commanded that their vessels be filled with grain, and that each man’s silver be restored to his sack, and that they be given provisions for the way. And thus it was done to them.
And they loaded the grain upon their donkeys, and departed from there.
And one opened his sack to give fodder to his donkeys where they lodged, and saw his bundle of silver; and it was at the mouth of the sack.

And he said to his brothers, “My silver is restored to me, and behold, it is in my sack.” And their hearts were astonished, and they were troubled, saying one to another, “What is this that God has done to us?”
And they came to Jacob their father in the land of Canaan, and told him all that had befallen them, saying,
“The man, the lord of the land, spoke harshly to us, and put us in custody as spies of the land.
“And we said to him, ‘We are peaceable men; we are no spies.
“‘We are twelve brothers, sons of our father; one is no more, and the youngest is with our father today in the land of Canaan.’

“And the man, the lord of the land, said to us, ‘By this I shall know that you are peaceable men: leave one brother here with me, and take the grain which you have bought for your household’s provision, and depart.
“‘And bring your youngest brother to me, and I shall know that you are no spies, but peaceable men; and I will restore your brother to you, and you may trade in the land.’”
And as they emptied their sacks, each man’s bundle of silver was in his sack; and they and their father saw their bundles of silver, and were afraid.
And Jacob their father said to them, “You have bereaved me of children. Joseph is no more, and Simeon is no more, and you will take Benjamin. All these things have come upon me.”
And Reuben said to his father, “Slay my two sons if I do not bring him to you. Give him into my hand, and I will bring him back to you.”

And he said, “My son shall not go down with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone is left; and if he should fall sick on the way which you go, you shall bring down my old age with sorrow into Hades.”
And the famine became severe in the land.
And when they had finished eating the grain which they brought from Egypt, their father said to them, “Go again and buy us a little food.”
And Judah said to him, “The man solemnly warned us, saying, ‘You shall not see my face unless your youngest brother is with you.’
“If therefore you send our brother with us, we will go down and buy you food.
“But if you do not send our brother with us, we will not go; for the man said to us, ‘You shall not see my face unless your youngest brother is with you.’”
And Israel said, “Why did you do me harm by telling the man that you had a brother?”

And they said, “The man questioned us closely concerning ourselves and our kindred, saying, ‘Is your father still living? Do you have a brother?’ And we told him according to this questioning. Could we know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother’?”
And Judah said to Israel his father, “Send the lad with me, and we will arise and go, that we may live and not die, both we and you and our households.
“I will stand as surety for him; require him from my hand. If I do not bring him to you and set him before you, I shall bear the guilt before you all my days.
“For if we had not delayed, we should by now have returned twice.”

And Israel their father said to them, “If it is so, do this: take some of the fruits of the land in your vessels, and carry down gifts to the man, resin and honey, spices and stacte, terebinth nuts and nuts.
“And take double the silver in your hands; the silver which was returned in your sacks, take back with you; perhaps it was an oversight.
“And take your brother, and arise and go down to the man.
“And may my God give you grace before the man, and may he release your other brother and Benjamin. As for me, as I am bereaved, I am bereaved.”
And the men took these gifts, and took double the silver in their hands, and Benjamin; and they rose and went down into Egypt, and stood before Joseph.

And Joseph saw them and Benjamin his brother, born of the same mother, and said to the steward of his house, “Bring the men into the house, and slaughter animals and prepare; for the men shall eat bread with me at noon.”
And the man did as Joseph said, and brought the men into Joseph’s house.

And the men saw that they were brought into Joseph’s house, and said, “Because of the silver which was returned in our sacks at first we are brought in, that he may falsely accuse us and fall upon us, and take us for slaves, and our donkeys.”
And they drew near to the steward of Joseph’s house, and spoke to him in the gateway of the house,
saying, “We beg you, my lord: we came down at first to buy food.
“And when we came to the lodging place and opened our sacks, behold, each man’s silver was in his sack. We have now brought back our silver in its full weight in our hands.
“And we have brought other silver with us to buy food. We do not know who put the silver into our sacks.”

And he said to them, “May you find favour; do not fear. Your God and the God of your fathers has given you treasures in your sacks; but I have received your good silver in full.” And he brought Simeon out to them,
and brought water to wash their feet, and gave fodder to their donkeys.
And they prepared the gifts until Joseph came at noon, for they heard that he was to dine there.
And Joseph came into the house, and they brought him the gifts which were in their hands into the house, and bowed down before him, with their faces to the earth.
And he asked them, “How are you?” And he said to them, “Is your aged father, of whom you spoke, well? Is he still living?”
And they said, “Your servant our father is well; he is still living.” And he said, “Blessed be that man by God.” And they bowed their heads and bowed down before him.

And Joseph lifted up his eyes and saw Benjamin his brother, born of the same mother, and said, “Is this your youngest brother, whom you said you would bring to me?” And he said, “May God show mercy to you, my child.”
And Joseph was troubled, for his inward parts were deeply stirred for his brother, and he sought to weep; and he entered his chamber and wept there.
And he washed his face and went out, and restrained himself, and said, “Set out the bread.”

And they served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who dined with him by themselves; for the Egyptians could not eat bread with the Hebrews, for it is an abomination to the Egyptians.
And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his seniority, and the youngest according to his youth; and the men marvelled one at another.
And portions were brought to them from him; but Benjamin’s portion was five times as great as the portions of them all. And they drank and became drunk with him.
And Joseph commanded the steward of his house, saying, “Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s silver at the mouth of his sack.
“And put my silver cup into the sack of the youngest, and the price of his grain.” And it was done according to Joseph’s word, as he had said.
The morning dawned, and the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.

And when they had gone out of the city, and were not far off, Joseph said to the steward of his house, “Arise, pursue the men, and you shall overtake them, and say to them, ‘Why have you repaid evil for good?
“‘Why have you stolen my silver cup? Is not this the cup from which my lord drinks? And with it he indeed practises divination. You have done evil in what you have done.’”
And he found them, and spoke to them these words.
And they said to him, “Why does my lord speak such words? Far be it from your servants to do such a thing.
“If we brought back to you from the land of Canaan the silver which we found in our sacks, how should we steal silver or gold from your lord’s house?
“With whomever of your servants the cup is found, let him die; and we also shall be slaves to our lord.”
And he said, “Now let it be as you say: the man with whom the cup is found shall be my slave, but you shall be clear of guilt.”
And they hurried, and each set down his sack upon the ground, and each opened his sack.
And he searched, beginning with the eldest until he came to the youngest; and he found the cup in Benjamin’s sack.
And they tore their garments, and each loaded his sack upon his donkey, and they returned to the city.
And Judah and his brothers came to Joseph while he was still there, and fell before him upon the earth.
And Joseph said to them, “What is this deed that you have done? Do you not know that a man such as I indeed practises divination?”

And Judah said, “What shall we answer to my lord, or what shall we speak, or how shall we be justified? God has found out the iniquity of your servants. Behold, we are household slaves to our lord, both we and he with whom the cup was found.”
And Joseph said, “Far be it from me to do this thing. The man with whom the cup was found shall be my slave; but you go up in safety to your father.”
And Judah drew near to him and said, “I beg you, my lord, let your servant speak a word before you, and do not be angry with your servant, for you are next to Pharaoh.
“My lord, you asked your servants, saying, ‘Do you have a father or a brother?’
“And we said to my lord, ‘We have an aged father, and a young son of his old age; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loves him.’
“And you said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, and I will care for him.’
“And we said to my lord, ‘The lad cannot leave his father; but if he leaves his father, he will die.’
“And you said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you shall see my face no more.’
“And when we went up to your servant our father, we told him the words of my lord.
“And our father said to us, ‘Go again, and buy us a little food.’
“And we said, ‘We cannot go down; but if our youngest brother goes down with us, we will go down. For we cannot see the man’s face unless our youngest brother is with us.’
“And your servant our father said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.
“‘And one went out from me, and you said, “He has been devoured by a beast”; and I have not seen him again to this day.
“‘If therefore you take this one also from my presence, and sickness befalls him on the way, you shall bring down my old age with sorrow into Hades.’
“Now therefore, if I come to your servant our father, and the lad is not with us, since his soul hangs upon the lad’s soul,
“when he sees that the lad is not with us, he will die; and your servants shall bring down the old age of your servant our father with anguish into Hades.
“For your servant became surety for the lad to his father, saying, ‘If I do not bring him to you and set him before you, I shall bear the guilt before my father all my days.’
“Now therefore I will remain with you as a servant in the lad’s place, a household slave to my lord; but let the lad go up with his brothers.
“For how shall I go up to my father if the lad is not with us? Let me not see the evils which shall befall my father.”
And Joseph could no longer bear all those who stood beside him, but said, “Send everyone away from me.” And no one else stood with Joseph when he made himself known to his brothers.
And he lifted up his voice with weeping; and all the Egyptians heard, and it was heard in Pharaoh’s house.
And Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph. Is my father still living?” And his brothers could not answer him, for they were troubled.
And Joseph said to his brothers, “Draw near to me.” And they drew near. And he said, “I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
“Now therefore do not be grieved, and do not let it seem hard to you that you sold me here; for God sent me before you to preserve life.
“For this is the second year of famine upon the land, and there are still five years left in which there shall be neither ploughing nor harvest.
“For God sent me before you, that a remnant of you might remain upon the earth, and to nourish a great remnant of you.
“Now therefore it was not you who sent me here, but God; and He has made me as a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler of all the land of Egypt.
“So hurry, and go up to my father, and say to him, ‘Thus says your son Joseph: God has made me lord of all the land of Egypt; come down therefore to me, and do not delay.
“‘And you shall live in the land of Goshen of Arabia, and shall be near to me, you and your sons and your sons’ sons, your sheep and your oxen, and all that you have.
“‘And I will nourish you there, for there are still five years of famine, lest you be destroyed, you and your sons and all your possessions.’
“Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of Benjamin my brother, that it is my mouth which speaks to you.
“Tell my father therefore of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that you have seen; and hurry and bring my father down here.”
And he fell upon the neck of Benjamin his brother, and wept over him; and Benjamin wept upon his neck.
And he kissed all his brothers, and wept over them; and afterward his brothers spoke with him.
And the report spread into Pharaoh’s house, saying, “Joseph’s brothers have come.” And Pharaoh and his attendants rejoiced.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Say to your brothers, ‘Do this: load your beasts, and depart to the land of Canaan.
“‘And take your father and your possessions, and come to me; and I will give you of all the good things of Egypt, and you shall eat the marrow of the land.’
“And give this command, that they take wagons from the land of Egypt: ‘Take them for your children and your wives, and bring your father, and come.
“‘And do not let your eyes regret your belongings, for all the good things of Egypt shall be yours.’”
And the sons of Israel did so; and Joseph gave them wagons according to the words of Pharaoh the king, and gave them provisions for the way.
And to them all he gave two robes each; but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of gold and five changes of robes.
And to his father he sent the same, and ten donkeys carrying some of all the good things of Egypt, and ten female mules carrying bread for his father’s journey.
And he sent his brothers away, and they departed; and he said to them, “Do not be angry on the way.”
And they went up from Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan to Jacob their father.
And they told him, saying, “Your son Joseph lives, and he rules all the land of Egypt.” And Jacob’s mind was astonished, for he did not believe them.
And they spoke to him all the words which Joseph had said to them. And when he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob their father was rekindled.
And Israel said, “It is a great thing to me if Joseph my son still lives. I will go and see him before I die.”
And Israel set out, he and all that he had, and came to the Well of the Oath, and offered a sacrifice to the God of his father Isaac.
And God spoke to Israel in a vision of the night, saying, “Jacob, Jacob.” And he said, “What is it?”
And He said, “I am the God of your fathers. Do not fear to go down into Egypt, for I will make you a great nation there.
“And I will go down with you into Egypt, and I will bring you up at last; and Joseph shall lay his hands upon your eyes.”
And Jacob rose from the Well of the Oath; and the sons of Israel carried their father and their households and their wives upon the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him.
And they took their possessions and all that they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and entered into Egypt, Jacob and all his seed with him,
his sons and his sons’ sons with him, his daughters and his sons’ daughters; and all his seed he brought into Egypt.
And these are the names of the sons of Israel who entered into Egypt, Jacob and his sons. Jacob’s firstborn was Reuben.
And Reuben’s sons: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
And Simeon’s sons: Jemuel, Jamin, Aod, Jachin, Saar, and Shaul the son of the Canaanite woman.
And Levi’s sons: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
And Judah’s sons: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah. But Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. And Perez’s sons were Hezron and Jemuel.
And Issachar’s sons: Tola, Phua, Jasoub, and Zambram.
And Zebulun’s sons: Sered, Allon, and Aloel.
These are Leah’s sons whom she bore to Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria, and Dinah his daughter. All the souls, sons and daughters, were thirty-three.
And Gad’s sons: Saphon, Haggis, Saunis, Thasoban, Aedis, Aroedis, and Aroelis.
And Asher’s sons: Jemna, Jesoua, Jeul, and Baria, and Sara their sister. And Baria’s sons: Chobor and Melchiel.
These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter; and she bore these to Jacob, sixteen souls.
And the sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife: Joseph and Benjamin.

And to Joseph were born sons in the land of Egypt, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, bore to him: Manasseh and Ephraim. And to Manasseh was born a son, whom his Syrian concubine bore to him, Machir; and Machir begot Gilead. And the sons of Ephraim, Manasseh’s brother: Soutalaam and Taam. And the sons of Soutalaam: Edem.
And Benjamin’s sons: Bala, Chobor, and Ashbel. And Bala’s sons were Gera, Noeman, Anchis, Ros, Mamphin, and Ophimin; and Gera begot Arad.
These are Rachel’s sons whom she bore to Jacob: all the souls were eighteen.
And the sons of Dan: Asom.
And Naphtali’s sons: Asiel, Gouni, Issaar, and Syllem.
These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter; and she bore these to Jacob: all the souls were seven.
And all the souls who entered into Egypt with Jacob, who came from his loins, apart from the wives of Jacob’s sons, were sixty-six souls in all.
And Joseph’s sons who were born to him in the land of Egypt were nine souls. All the souls of Jacob’s house who entered into Egypt were seventy-five.
And he sent Judah before him to Joseph, to meet him near Heroopolis in the land of Rameses.
And Joseph harnessed his chariots, and went up to meet Israel his father near Heroopolis; and he appeared to him, and fell upon his neck, and wept abundantly.
And Israel said to Joseph, “Now I may die, since I have seen your face, for you are still alive.”
And Joseph said to his brothers, “I will go up and tell Pharaoh, and say to him, ‘My brothers and my father’s house, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.
“‘And the men are shepherds, for they have been keepers of livestock; and they have brought their livestock and their oxen and all that they have.’
“If therefore Pharaoh calls you, and says to you, ‘What is your work?’

“you shall say, ‘Your servants have been keepers of livestock from youth until now, both we and our fathers,’ that you may live in the land of Goshen of Arabia; for every shepherd of sheep is an abomination to the Egyptians.”

And Joseph came and told Pharaoh, saying, “My father and my brothers, and their livestock and their oxen and all that they have, have come from the land of Canaan; and behold, they are in the land of Goshen.”
And he took five men from among his brothers, and set them before Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph’s brothers, “What is your work?” And they said to Pharaoh, “Your servants are shepherds of sheep, both we and our fathers.”

And they said to Pharaoh, “We have come to live as strangers in the land; for there is no pasture for your servants’ livestock, because the famine has become severe in the land of Canaan. Now therefore your servants will live in the land of Goshen.”

And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Let them live in the land of Goshen; and if you know that there are able men among them, set them over my livestock.” And Jacob and his sons came into Egypt to Joseph; and Pharaoh king of Egypt heard. And Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, “Your father and your brothers have come to you.
“Behold, the land of Egypt is before you; settle your father and your brothers in the best of the land.”
And Joseph brought in Jacob his father, and set him before Pharaoh; and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to Jacob, “How many are the years of the days of your life?”

And Jacob said to Pharaoh, “The days of the years of my life in which I sojourn are a hundred and thirty years. Few and grievous have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not reached the days of the years of the life of my fathers, in the days when they sojourned.”
And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from him.
And Joseph settled his father and his brothers, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh commanded.
And Joseph measured out grain to his father and to his brothers and to all his father’s house, according to each person.
And there was no grain in all the land, for the famine had become exceedingly severe; and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan languished because of the famine.

And Joseph gathered all the silver found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan for the grain which they bought, and he measured it out to them; and Joseph brought all the silver into Pharaoh’s house.
And all the silver in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan was spent. And all the Egyptians came to Joseph, saying, “Give us bread; why should we die before you? For our silver is spent.”
And Joseph said to them, “Bring your livestock, and I will give you bread in exchange for your livestock, if the silver is spent.”

And they brought their livestock to Joseph; and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for their horses and sheep and oxen and donkeys, and nourished them with bread in exchange for all their livestock that year.

And that year ended, and they came to him in the second year, and said to him, “Let us not be destroyed before our lord. For if our silver is spent, and our possessions and livestock have passed to you, our lord, there remains nothing to us before our lord except our own bodies and our land.

“Therefore, lest we die before you and the land become desolate, buy us and our land in exchange for bread, and we and our land shall be Pharaoh’s slaves. Give us seed, that we may sow and live and not die, and the land shall not be desolate.”
And Joseph bought all the land of the Egyptians for Pharaoh; for the Egyptians sold their land to Pharaoh, because the famine prevailed over them. And the land became Pharaoh’s.
And he enslaved the people to him as slaves, from one end of the borders of Egypt to the other.

The land of the priests was the only land Joseph did not buy; for Pharaoh gave an allowance to the priests, and they ate of the allowance which Pharaoh gave them. Therefore they did not sell their land.
And Joseph said to all the Egyptians, “Behold, I have bought you and your land today for Pharaoh. Take seed for yourselves, and sow the land.
“And of its produce you shall give a fifth part to Pharaoh; but the four parts shall be yours, for seed for the land, and for food for you and for all who are in your houses.”
And they said, “You have saved us; we have found grace before our lord, and we shall be Pharaoh’s slaves.”
And Joseph established this for them as an ordinance concerning the land of Egypt to this day, to give a fifth to Pharaoh, except only the land of the priests, which was not Pharaoh’s.
And Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; and they obtained possessions in it, and increased and multiplied exceedingly.
And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years; and the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred and forty-seven years.

And the days drew near when Israel must die; and he called Joseph his son, and said to him, “If I have found grace in your sight, put your hand under my thigh, and show mercy and truth to me: do not bury me in Egypt.
“But I will sleep with my fathers, and you shall carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their tomb.” And he said, “I will do according to your word.”
And he said, “Swear to me.” And he swore to him. And Israel bowed in worship upon the top of his staff.
And after these things Joseph was told, “Your father is ailing.” And he took his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, and came to Jacob.
And it was told to Jacob, saying, “Behold, your son Joseph comes to you.” And Israel strengthened himself, and sat upon the bed.
And Jacob said to Joseph, “My God appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me.
“And He said to me, ‘Behold, I will increase you and multiply you, and make you assemblies of nations; and I will give this land to you and to your seed after you for an everlasting possession.’
“Now therefore your two sons who were born to you in Egypt before I came to you into Egypt are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine, as Reuben and Simeon.
“But the children whom you beget after them shall be yours; they shall be called by the names of their brothers within their allotments.

“And when I came from Mesopotamia of Syria, Rachel your mother died in the land of Canaan, as I drew near to the horse-course of Chabratha in the land, on the way to Ephrath; and I buried her on the road of the horse-course, which is Bethlehem.”
And Israel saw Joseph’s sons, and said, “Who are these with you?”
And Joseph said to his father, “They are my sons, whom God has given me here.” And Jacob said, “Bring them to me, that I may bless them.”
And Israel’s eyes were dim with age, and he could not see; and he brought them near to him, and he kissed and embraced them.
And Israel said to Joseph, “Behold, I have not been deprived of your face; and behold, God has shown me your seed also.”
And Joseph brought them out from his knees, and they bowed down before him, with their faces to the earth.
And Joseph took his two sons, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel’s left, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel’s right, and brought them near to him.
And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim’s head, though he was the younger, and his left hand upon Manasseh’s head, crossing his hands.
And he blessed them, and said, “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac were well pleasing, the God who has nourished me from my youth to this day,

“the angel who delivers me from all evils, bless these children; and my name shall be called upon them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and may they multiply into a great multitude upon the earth.”
And Joseph saw that his father had laid his right hand upon Ephraim’s head, and it displeased him; and Joseph took hold of his father’s hand, to remove it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s head.
And Joseph said to his father, “Not so, father; for this is the firstborn. Lay your right hand upon his head.”

And he would not, but said, “I know, my child, I know. He also shall become a people, and he also shall be exalted; but his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations.”
And he blessed them that day, saying, “In you shall Israel be blessed, saying, ‘May God make you as Ephraim and as Manasseh.’” And he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
And Israel said to Joseph, “Behold, I am dying; and God shall be with you, and shall bring you back to the land of your fathers.
“And I give to you Shechem as a choice portion above your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorites with my sword and bow.”
And Jacob called his sons, and said, “Gather yourselves, that I may tell you what shall befall you in the latter days.
“Assemble and hear, you sons of Jacob; listen to Israel your father.
“Reuben, you are my firstborn, my strength and the beginning of my children, hard to bear and stubbornly self-willed.
“You overflowed in insolence as water; do not boil over. For you went up to your father’s bed; then you defiled the couch where you went up.
“Simeon and Levi are brothers; they committed iniquity by their own choice.
“Do not let my soul enter their council, or my inward parts rest upon their conspiracy; for in their wrath they slew men, and in their desire they hamstrung a bull.
“Cursed be their wrath, for it is self-willed, and their anger, for it is hardened. I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel.
“Judah, may your brothers praise you; your hands shall be upon the backs of your enemies, and your father’s sons shall bow down to you.
“Judah is a lion’s cub. From a shoot, my son, you have gone up. You reclined and slept as a lion, and as a cub; who shall rouse him?
“A ruler shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until the things reserved for him come; and he shall be the expectation of nations.
“Binding his foal to the vine, and his donkey’s colt to the tendril, he shall wash his robe in wine, and his mantle in the blood of the grape.
“His eyes are joyful from wine, and his teeth whiter than milk.
“Zebulun shall dwell by the sea, and beside a haven of ships, and shall extend to Sidon.
“Issachar desired that which is good, resting between the allotments.
“And he saw that rest was good, and the land rich; and he bent his shoulder to toil, and became a tiller of the earth.
“Dan shall judge his own people, as one tribe in Israel.
“And let Dan become a serpent by the way, lying in wait upon the path, biting the horse’s heel; and the rider shall fall backward.
“I wait for the salvation of the Lord.
“Gad, a raiding band shall raid him, but he shall raid at their heels.
“Asher, his bread shall be rich, and he shall give delicacies to rulers.
“Naphtali is a spreading tree, yielding beauty in its fruit.
“Joseph is a son grown great, a son grown great, envied; my youngest son, return to me.
“They plotted against him and reviled him; and the masters of arrows bore him a grudge.
“And their bows were mightily shattered, and the sinews of their arms grew slack, by the hand of the Mighty One of Jacob; from there is He who strengthened Israel,

“from the God of your father; and my God helped you, and blessed you with the blessing of heaven above, and the blessing of the earth which holds all things, because of the blessing of breasts and womb,

“the blessing of your father and your mother. It prevailed over the blessings of enduring mountains and the blessings of everlasting dunes. They shall be upon Joseph’s head, and upon the crown of the brothers whom he led.
“Benjamin is a ravening wolf; in the morning he shall yet eat, and toward evening he shall distribute food.”
All these are Jacob’s twelve sons; and these things their father spoke to them, and blessed them. He blessed them, each according to his blessing.
And he said to them, “I am being added to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave which is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
“in the double cave opposite Mamre in the land of Canaan, the cave which Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite for a burial possession.
“There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah,
“in the possession of the field and the cave within it, acquired from the sons of Heth.”
And Jacob ceased charging his sons; and he drew up his feet upon the bed, and died, and was added to his people.
And Joseph fell upon his father’s face, and wept over him, and kissed him.
And Joseph commanded his servants the embalmers to prepare his father for burial; and the embalmers prepared Israel for burial.
And they fulfilled forty days for him, for this is how the days of burial preparation are reckoned; and Egypt mourned him seventy days.
And when the days of mourning had passed, Joseph spoke to Pharaoh’s rulers, saying, “If I have found grace in your sight, speak concerning me in Pharaoh’s ears, saying,
“‘My father made me swear, saying, “In the tomb which I dug for myself in the land of Canaan, there you shall bury me.” Now therefore I will go up and bury my father, and return.’”
And Pharaoh said, “Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear.”
And Joseph went up to bury his father; and with him went up all Pharaoh’s servants, and the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
and all Joseph’s household, and his brothers, and all his father’s house; but they left their kindred and their sheep and their oxen in the land of Goshen.
And chariots and horsemen also went up with him, and the company was exceedingly great.
And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan; and they lamented him with a great and exceedingly grievous lamentation, and he mourned his father seven days.

And the inhabitants of the land of Canaan saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, and said, “This is a great mourning for the Egyptians.” Therefore its name was called Mourning of Egypt, which is beyond the Jordan.
And his sons did thus to him, and buried him there.
And his sons carried him up into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the double cave, the cave which Abraham bought for a burial possession from Ephron the Hittite, opposite Mamre.
And Joseph returned into Egypt, he and his brothers and those who had gone up to bury his father.
And Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, and said, “What if Joseph should bear a grudge against us, and fully repay us all the evils which we did to him?”
And they came to Joseph, saying, “Your father gave a charge by oath before he died, saying,

“‘This is what you shall say to Joseph: “Forgive them their iniquity and their sin, for they did evil to you.”’ And now, pardon the iniquity of the servants of your father’s God.” And Joseph wept as they spoke to him.
And they came to him, and said, “Behold, we are your household slaves.”
And Joseph said to them, “Do not fear, for I belong to God.
“You planned evil against me, but God planned good concerning me, that it might come to pass as it is today, that many people might be fed.”
And he said to them, “Do not fear; I will nourish you and your households.” And he comforted them, and spoke to their hearts.
And Joseph lived in Egypt, he and his brothers and all his father’s household; and Joseph lived a hundred and ten years.
And Joseph saw Ephraim’s children to the third generation; and the sons of Machir, Manasseh’s son, were born upon Joseph’s thighs.
And Joseph spoke to his brothers, saying, “I am dying; but God shall surely visit you, and bring you up from this land to the land which God swore to our fathers Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.”
And Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying, “In the visitation with which God shall visit you, you shall carry up my bones from here with you.”
And Joseph died, being a hundred and ten years old; and they performed his burial rites, and laid him in a coffin in Egypt.
